content.content:
### F-015 · Före/efter-delaren är ett referensmönster, inte ett helsideskoncept
- **Visades:** K4-r8 på boarden, hela sidan: den tippande delaren mellan
  `sites/before-ai-slop.html` och Calyx, R3-läget med plan 004 öppen.
- **Antons ord (ur beställningen 2026-09-15, återgivet):** K4-slidern från förra sessionen
  sparas som referens för den typen av före/efter-showcase, inte som helsideskoncept.
  Huvuduppgiften är i stället K3:s ritning som processakt i V3-sidan.
- **Dom:** hade kunnat bli bra som del, inte som helhet. Delaren som mekanik håller
  (två hela sidor i miniatyr, ps 0,40 med Calyx som vyns största objekt, verified i R3);
  som bärande idé för en hel byråsida räcker den inte.
- **Regel:** en showcase-mekanik som bevisar ett påstående (före/efter) är ett
  *mönster* i katalogen av egna akter, inte ett koncept. Den får återanvändas som en
  sektion i en sida vars grammatik bär den; den bygger ingen sida ensam. K4-cellen
  parkeras som det mönstret, med sin BRIEF, NOTES och `?preview=`-lägen som
  referensmaterial. Plan 004 (bildtexten klipps under 640) förblir öppen och stänger
  inte cellen, eftersom cellen inte längre ska skeppas.
- **Status:** bara här, plus raden i `tests/alunix-r8/STATUS.md` och `runs/K4/NOTES.md`.

## 2026-09-19 · Antons stående förbud, ingen board — läst direkt av Alunix-sidan

### F-016 · Liten "beskrivande" stiltypisk AI-text är helt förbjuden
- **Visades:** ingen board. Antons ord är ett stående beslut, inte en dom över en
  körning, men han pekade konkret på Alunix-sidan (`tests/alunix-r8`): små
  kickers/eyebrows ("EXEMPELCASE", "FRÅN EXEMPEL TILL ER SIDA", "SÅ GÅR DET TILL"),
  bildtexter ("Exempelsida: Hōrai, Asian fusion-koncept", "Exempelsida: Calyx, florist
  i Stockholm"), sidomenyer som listar stegrubriker i liten grå text, och små
  förklarande rader under rubriker i liten storlek ("Första steget är ett samtal om
  vad ni gör.").
- **Antons ord:** "All sån liten 'beskrivande' stiltypisk AI-text är härmed helt
  förbjuden och jag vill att designsystemet härmed aktivt arbetar emot det och kollar
  efter det i befintliga sidor."
- **Dom:** dåligt, generellt — inte begränsat till Alunix-cellen som visade det.
- **Regel:** ingen liten text vars enda jobb är att fylla, förklara det uppenbara,
  eller se designad ut. Testet: gör raden ett jobb läsaren behöver (identifierar,
  differentierar, lokaliserar eller möjliggör en handling), eller talar den bara om
  sidan/exemplet i mindre storlek än brödtexten? Det senare tas bort. Antons uttryckliga
  undantag: en sajts egen genre-apparat som är stilenlig OCH bär en funktion i den
  genren är inte utfyllnad — Calyx tidskriftsapparat (utgåva, löpnummer, plats-index)
  och Hōrais avsiktliga etiketter (rätt-namn, servis-nummer) identifierar verkliga
  saker på riktiga sajter i den genren; en digital byrås demo-sida i Alunix genre har
  ingen sådan licens.
- **Status:** portad till `anti-patterns.md` § Descriptive microtext (gate 99),
  `production-tells.md` gate 99, `gates.md`, SKILL.md § Apparatus (marknadssidor:
  default noll), kontroll `skills/design/scripts/microtext_scan.py`,
  `design-catalogue/MICROTEXT-AUDIT.md`.

### F-017 · Prisliggarens displaystorlek är bara för siffror, inte för texten bredvid
- **Visades:** ingen board — samma session, prisliggarmönstret i katalogen
  (`house-physics.md` § Ledger, redan i bruk i Calyx/Hyperborea).
- **Antons ord (parafraserat i beställningen, samma dag):** displaystorlek i en
  priskolumn är bara för siffror (kompakta figurer som bildar rytm); text i samma
  kolumn ("Pris vid förfrågan") sätts ett steg mindre och linjeras mot siffrornas
  baslinje; en kontaktrad storleksätts som en handling, inte som en rubrik.
- **Dom:** regel, inte ett fel som redan visats — katalogens befintliga ledgers
  (Calyx, Hyperborea) skrevs redan så (siffra i display, valuta i kicker), men
  regeln stod inte skriven separat från valutaetiketten, så en textrad ("Pris vid
  förfrågan", "Kontakta oss") kunde av misstag ärva samma display-storlek som
  priset. Skrivs ner nu så nästa bygge inte chansar.
- **Regel:** i en ledger-rad bär enbart siffercellen display-storleken; en textcell i
  samma kolumn (`"Pris vid förfrågan"`, en enhet, en villkorstext) sätts ett
  typografiskt steg mindre än siffran och baslinjelinjeras mot den, aldrig
  samma storlek. En kontaktrad (telefon, mejl, boka-länk) storlekssätts som en
  handling — knapptext- eller länkstorlek — aldrig som en rubrik.
- **Status:** portad till `house-physics.md` § Ledger, never card grid, kontrollen
  `microtext_scan.py --price-ledger`.

### F-018 · Sidan får aldrig berätta vad den strax ska göra
- **Visades:** boardgranskning 2026-09-20, Alunix V3d (`tests/alunix-r8`), ingressen
  under kapitelrubriken Exempelcase: "Calyx är en florist i Stockholm och Hōrai en
  restaurang. Ingen av dem finns, men sidorna är färdiga. Vi går igenom vad vi valde i
  dem och varför."
- **Antons ord:** "är återigen helt hjärndött, och precis samma AI-slop som jag
  reagerade på tidigare."
- **Dom:** dåligt, generellt. Samma familj som F-016, men en annan storlek: detta är
  brödtext, inte småtext, så `microtext_scan.py` ser den aldrig.
- **Diagnos, tre drag som bär felet:**
  1. **Färdplanen.** "Vi går igenom vad vi valde i dem och varför" beskriver sidans
     egen disposition. En läsare som ser en case-sektion vet redan att den innehåller
     case; raden talar om formen i stället för att säga något.
  2. **Brasklappen.** "Ingen av dem finns" ber om ursäkt för arbetet innan det visats,
     och sänker det läsaren just ska bedöma.
  3. **Uppställningen.** Formen uppställning → brasklapp → färdplan är LLM-default för
     "introducera ett avsnitt" och känns igen på sitt tempo, inte på sina ord.
- **Regel:** ingen text på sidan refererar till sidan. En ingress, en kicker eller en
  inledande rad handlar om verksamheten, arbetet eller läsarens fråga — aldrig om vad
  avsnittet nedanför innehåller, i vilken ordning det kommer, eller varför det finns.
  Ingen brasklapp om materialets status före materialet. Testet: stryk raden och se om
  läsaren tappar något annat än en beskrivning av det hen ändå ser. Gör hen inte det,
  var raden utfyllnad — och ett avsnitt som bara har en rubrik ska hellre sättas så att
  rubriken bär ensam än förses med en ingress som fyller ut.
- **Status:** portad till `anti-patterns.md` § Descriptive microtext (ny underrubrik
  § The page narrating itself), `production-tells.md` gate 99, `gates.md` gate 99,
  `skills/design/references/copy-gate.md`.

## 2026-09-25 · r8-boarden (port 4626), V3g "Rutverket · mjuk showcase" runda 2

### F-019 · Textrutans rubrik får inte ta över
- **Visades:** V3g R2, showcasens textruta på desktop med stegrubriken i cirka 120 px
  (`En mening som saktar in`, `Ett mejl räcker`) över ett stort skuggat stegtal (`03`, `05`).
- **Antons ord:** "showcasen är bättre men rubriken är alldeles för stor och ger inte önskad
  effekt, det tar över på ett dåligt sätt, testa en annan layout på texten men behåll
  mekanismen."
- **Dom:** mekanismen bra (övertoning, räknare, mintspår), typografin i rutan dålig.
- **Regel:** i en ruta som följer en levande sajt är sajten huvudsaken och texten
  bildtexten. Stegrubriken står i rubrikskala (h3, ungefär 28–32 px), inte i displayskala.
  Rutans tomma yta fylls med innehåll, aldrig med förstorad text eller jättesiffror, och
  aldrig med ornament (se F-022, som upphäver den tidigare formuleringen "fylls med struktur").
- **Status:** V3g EFFECTS.md, runda 3-briefen.

### F-020 · Scrollen går för fort, och mjukheten får inte offras för farten
- **Visades:** V3g R2, hela sidan med Lenis-standard (ett hjulsteg = 100 px) och hero-pinnen
  `+=120%`.
- **Antons ord:** "när man scrollar ned en gång på hjulet så hoppar man ned från toppen av
  sidan och kastas förbi kortet så man knappt hinner se det vändas … tvinga sakta ned
  scrollen … var extra noga med att se till att den är mjuk och jämn hela vägen." Om
  showcasen: "den hoppar ned för sidan väldigt hastigt mellan texterna."
- **Dom:** dåligt, generellt.
- **Regel:** husets tempo är `wheelMultiplier: 0.6`, `lerp: 0.075`. En pin vars innehåll
  läsaren ska se ske spänner minst 200 vh. Den inbäddade sajten glider mellan ankare över
  större delen av segmentet, aldrig i ett ryck. Allt verifieras jämnt med `section_probe.py`.
- **Status:** `references/scroll/devices.md` § Load-bearing rules.

### F-021 · En bra effekt försämrades av en ändring någon annanstans
- **Visades:** V3g R2 mot V3f. Tesrubriken "Det första intrycket är digitalt." var orörd i
  koden men märkbart mer statisk och ryckig.
- **Antons ord:** "var också bättre förra rundan, nu är den mer statisk och ryckig. Ta reda
  på anledningen … systemet får inte ta fel på bra effekter och göra de sämre, agenterna
  måste ha tydliga instruktioner och riktlinjer för vad som är bra."
- **Grundorsak (mätt):** iframes i en pinnad scen laddades om vid varje
  `ScrollTrigger.refresh()`, eftersom pin-spacern flyttar dem i DOM:en. Varje omladdning bad
  om en ny refresh, och loopen gick hela besöket: 6–12 omladdningar per iframe per pass.
  Felet fanns redan i V3f. R2 förladdade den andra sajten och dubblade kostnaden, och tesens
  p95 gick från 33 till 50–100 ms.
- **Regel:** godkända effekter skyddas. De står i körningens `EFFECTS.md` med en uppmätt
  signatur. Varje runda kör `section_probe.py` på HELA sidan mot baslinjen, och en sektion
  som blivit sämre blockerar rundan även om ingen rad i den ändrats. En iframe i en pin
  kräver en egen `pinSpacer`, och en refresh anropas aldrig från en iframes `load`.
- **Status:** `references/motion.md` § Approved effects are protected,
  `references/scroll/devices.md`, `scripts/section_probe.py`.

### F-022 · Dekorativa streck läses som ofärdig kod
- **Visades:** V3g R4–R5, showcasens textruta med en lodrät "stegskala" (tunn linje, fem–sex
  streck, glidande mintmarkör) som skulle bära rutans höjd. Specen var leadens egen (R3), och
  leaden godkände den själv på skärmbild.
- **Antons ord:** "Hur godkändes de gröna strecken? Det ser ut som något ofärdigt som släppts
  igenom koden. Det räcker med att flytta upp stycket istället, men hela utseendet på det ser
  fortfarande för platt ut, lös det."
- **Dom:** dåligt, generellt.
- **Regel:** ett element som inte bär innehåll och inte är ett godkänt husgrepp (rastret,
  cellnätet, mintlinjen som markering) byggs inte för att fylla yta. Tom yta är ett
  kompositionsproblem: flytta innehållet, eller ge ytan riktigt innehåll (bild, detalj ur
  arbetet). "Det syns i alla fall" räcker inte som godkännande. Leadens egen spec granskas med
  samma fråga som byggarens: skulle Anton se det här som färdigt?
- **Status:** V3g runda 6-briefen; `references/motion.md` § Approved effects (leaden är inte
  undantagen).

### F-015 · Före/efter-delaren är ett referensmönster, inte ett helsideskoncept
- **Visades:** K4-r8 på boarden, hela sidan: den tippande delaren mellan
  `sites/before-ai-slop.html` och Calyx, R3-läget med plan 004 öppen.
- **Antons ord (ur beställningen 2026-09-15, återgivet):** K4-slidern från förra sessionen
  sparas som referens för den typen av före/efter-showcase, inte som helsideskoncept.
  Huvuduppgiften är i stället K3:s ritning som processakt i V3-sidan.
- **Dom:** hade kunnat bli bra som del, inte som helhet. Delaren som mekanik håller
  (två hela sidor i miniatyr, ps 0,40 med Calyx som vyns största objekt, verified i R3);
  som bärande idé för en hel byråsida räcker den inte.
- **Regel:** en showcase-mekanik som bevisar ett påstående (före/efter) är ett
  *mönster* i katalogen av egna akter, inte ett koncept. Den får återanvändas som en
  sektion i en sida vars grammatik bär den; den bygger ingen sida ensam. K4-cellen
  parkeras som det mönstret, med sin BRIEF, NOTES och `?preview=`-lägen som
  referensmaterial. Plan 004 (bildtexten klipps under 640) förblir öppen och stänger
  inte cellen, eftersom cellen inte längre ska skeppas.
- **Status:** bara här, plus raden i `tests/alunix-r8/STATUS.md` och `runs/K4/NOTES.md`.

## 2026-09-19 · Antons stående förbud, ingen board — läst direkt av Alunix-sidan

### F-016 · Liten "beskrivande" stiltypisk AI-text är helt förbjuden
- **Visades:** ingen board. Antons ord är ett stående beslut, inte en dom över en
  körning, men han pekade konkret på Alunix-sidan (`tests/alunix-r8`): små
  kickers/eyebrows ("EXEMPELCASE", "FRÅN EXEMPEL TILL ER SIDA", "SÅ GÅR DET TILL"),
  bildtexter ("Exempelsida: Hōrai, Asian fusion-koncept", "Exempelsida: Calyx, florist
  i Stockholm"), sidomenyer som listar stegrubriker i liten grå text, och små
  förklarande rader under rubriker i liten storlek ("Första steget är ett samtal om
  vad ni gör.").
- **Antons ord:** "All sån liten 'beskrivande' stiltypisk AI-text är härmed helt
  förbjuden och jag vill att designsystemet härmed aktivt arbetar emot det och kollar
  efter det i befintliga sidor."
- **Dom:** dåligt, generellt — inte begränsat till Alunix-cellen som visade det.
- **Regel:** ingen liten text vars enda jobb är att fylla, förklara det uppenbara,
  eller se designad ut. Testet: gör raden ett jobb läsaren behöver (identifierar,
  differentierar, lokaliserar eller möjliggör en handling), eller talar den bara om
  sidan/exemplet i mindre storlek än brödtexten? Det senare tas bort. Antons uttryckliga
  undantag: en sajts egen genre-apparat som är stilenlig OCH bär en funktion i den
  genren är inte utfyllnad — Calyx tidskriftsapparat (utgåva, löpnummer, plats-index)
  och Hōrais avsiktliga etiketter (rätt-namn, servis-nummer) identifierar verkliga
  saker på riktiga sajter i den genren; en digital byrås demo-sida i Alunix genre har
  ingen sådan licens.
- **Status:** portad till `anti-patterns.md` § Descriptive microtext (gate 99),
  `production-tells.md` gate 99, `gates.md`, SKILL.md § Apparatus (marknadssidor:
  default noll), kontroll `skills/design/scripts/microtext_scan.py`,
  `design-catalogue/MICROTEXT-AUDIT.md`.

### F-017 · Prisliggarens displaystorlek är bara för siffror, inte för texten bredvid
- **Visades:** ingen board — samma session, prisliggarmönstret i katalogen
  (`house-physics.md` § Ledger, redan i bruk i Calyx/Hyperborea).
- **Antons ord (parafraserat i beställningen, samma dag):** displaystorlek i en
  priskolumn är bara för siffror (kompakta figurer som bildar rytm); text i samma
  kolumn ("Pris vid förfrågan") sätts ett steg mindre och linjeras mot siffrornas
  baslinje; en kontaktrad storleksätts som en handling, inte som en rubrik.
- **Dom:** regel, inte ett fel som redan visats — katalogens befintliga ledgers
  (Calyx, Hyperborea) skrevs redan så (siffra i display, valuta i kicker), men
  regeln stod inte skriven separat från valutaetiketten, så en textrad ("Pris vid
  förfrågan", "Kontakta oss") kunde av misstag ärva samma display-storlek som
  priset. Skrivs ner nu så nästa bygge inte chansar.
- **Regel:** i en ledger-rad bär enbart siffercellen display-storleken; en textcell i
  samma kolumn (`"Pris vid förfrågan"`, en enhet, en villkorstext) sätts ett
  typografiskt steg mindre än siffran och baslinjelinjeras mot den, aldrig
  samma storlek. En kontaktrad (telefon, mejl, boka-länk) storlekssätts som en
  handling — knapptext- eller länkstorlek — aldrig som en rubrik.
- **Status:** portad till `house-physics.md` § Ledger, never card grid, kontrollen
  `microtext_scan.py --price-ledger`.

### F-018 · Sidan får aldrig berätta vad den strax ska göra
- **Visades:** boardgranskning 2026-09-20, Alunix V3d (`tests/alunix-r8`), ingressen
  under kapitelrubriken Exempelcase: "Calyx är en florist i Stockholm och Hōrai en
  restaurang. Ingen av dem finns, men sidorna är färdiga. Vi går igenom vad vi valde i
  dem och varför."
- **Antons ord:** "är återigen helt hjärndött, och precis samma AI-slop som jag
  reagerade på tidigare."
- **Dom:** dåligt, generellt. Samma familj som F-016, men en annan storlek: detta är
  brödtext, inte småtext, så `microtext_scan.py` ser den aldrig.
- **Diagnos, tre drag som bär felet:**
  1. **Färdplanen.** "Vi går igenom vad vi valde i dem och varför" beskriver sidans
     egen disposition. En läsare som ser en case-sektion vet redan att den innehåller
     case; raden talar om formen i stället för att säga något.
  2. **Brasklappen.** "Ingen av dem finns" ber om ursäkt för arbetet innan det visats,
     och sänker det läsaren just ska bedöma.
  3. **Uppställningen.** Formen uppställning → brasklapp → färdplan är LLM-default för
     "introducera ett avsnitt" och känns igen på sitt tempo, inte på sina ord.
- **Regel:** ingen text på sidan refererar till sidan. En ingress, en kicker eller en
  inledande rad handlar om verksamheten, arbetet eller läsarens fråga — aldrig om vad
  avsnittet nedanför innehåller, i vilken ordning det kommer, eller varför det finns.
  Ingen brasklapp om materialets status före materialet. Testet: stryk raden och se om
  läsaren tappar något annat än en beskrivning av det hen ändå ser. Gör hen inte det,
  var raden utfyllnad — och ett avsnitt som bara har en rubrik ska hellre sättas så att
  rubriken bär ensam än förses med en ingress som fyller ut.
- **Status:** portad till `anti-patterns.md` § Descriptive microtext (ny underrubrik
  § The page narrating itself), `production-tells.md` gate 99, `gates.md` gate 99,
  `skills/design/references/copy-gate.md`.

## 2026-09-25 · r8-boarden (port 4626), V3g "Rutverket · mjuk showcase" runda 2

### F-019 · Textrutans rubrik får inte ta över
- **Visades:** V3g R2, showcasens textruta på desktop med stegrubriken i cirka 120 px
  (`En mening som saktar in`, `Ett mejl räcker`) över ett stort skuggat stegtal (`03`, `05`).
- **Antons ord:** "showcasen är bättre men rubriken är alldeles för stor och ger inte önskad
  effekt, det tar över på ett dåligt sätt, testa en annan layout på texten men behåll
  mekanismen."
- **Dom:** mekanismen bra (övertoning, räknare, mintspår), typografin i rutan dålig.

  `+=120%`.
- **Antons ord:** "när man scrollar ned en gång på hjulet så hoppar man ned från toppen av
  sidan och kastas förbi kortet så man knappt hinner se det vändas … tvinga sakta ned

  showcasen: "den hoppar ned för sidan väldigt hastigt mellan texterna."
- **Dom:** dåligt, generellt.
- **Regel:** husets tempo är `wheelMultiplier: 0.6`, `lerp: 0.075`. En pin vars innehåll

  större delen av segmentet, aldrig i ett ryck. Allt verifieras jämnt med `section_probe.py`.
- **Status:** `references/scroll/devices.md` § Load-bearing rules.

### F-021 · En bra effekt försämrades av en ändring någon annanstans

  koden men märkbart mer statisk och ryckig.
- **Antons ord:** "var också bättre förra rundan, nu är den mer statisk och ryckig. Ta reda
  på anledningen … systemet får inte ta fel på bra effekter och göra de sämre, agenterna

<!doctype html>
<html lang="sv">
<head>
<meta charset="utf-8">
<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width,initial-scale=1">
<title>ALUNIX</title>
<link rel="stylesheet" href="assets/vendor/lenis.css">

<style>
@font-face{
  font-family:"Geist";
  src:url("assets/fonts/geist-500-latin.woff2") format("woff2");
  font-weight:500; font-style:normal; font-display:swap;
}
@font-face{
  font-family:"Geist Mono";
  src:url("assets/fonts/geist-mono-400-latin.woff2") format("woff2");
  font-weight:400; font-style:normal; font-display:swap;
}

:root{
  --paper:#ffffff;
  --ink:#232323;
  --black:#000000;
  --grey:#d9d9d9;
  --mint:#0af474;
  --mint-soft:#a3fbcb;
  --rust:#9c5a3a;
  --lacquer:#b23524;
  --seam:1px solid #000;

  --headline-50:clamp(3.25rem, 0.418rem + 12.082vw, 12.5rem);
  --headline-40:clamp(2.5rem, 1.352rem + 4.9vw, 6.25rem);
  --headline-20:clamp(2rem, 1.694rem + 1.306vw, 3rem);
  --h3:38px;
  --body:16px;
  --body-30:clamp(1.5rem, 1.347rem + 0.653vw, 2rem);
  --caption:13px;
  --cellpad:20px;
}

*{box-sizing:border-box;}
html{color-scheme:light;}
body{
  margin:0;
  background:#000;
  color:var(--ink);
  font-family:"Geist","Arial",system-ui,sans-serif;
  font-weight:500;
  line-height:1.3;
  -webkit-font-smoothing:antialiased;
  overflow-x:hidden;
}
img{display:block;max-width:100%;}
.mono{font-family:"Geist Mono","Consolas",monospace;font-weight:400;}
h1,h2,h3,p,ol,ul,figure{margin:0;padding:0;}
a{color:inherit;}
.sr-only{position:absolute;width:1px;height:1px;padding:0;margin:-1px;overflow:hidden;clip:rect(0,0,0,0);white-space:nowrap;border:0;}

/* ---------------------------------------------------------- rutverket shell */
.rutverk{max-width:1440px;margin:0 auto;background:#000;}
.rutverk > section{scroll-margin-top:48px;}

.g{display:grid;gap:1px;background:#000;}
.cell{background:var(--paper);padding:var(--cellpad);position:relative;overflow:hidden;}
.cell--pad0{padding:0;}
.cell--ink{background:var(--ink);color:var(--paper);}
.cell--black{background:var(--black);color:var(--paper);}
.cell--grey{background:var(--grey);color:var(--ink);}
.cell--mint{background:var(--mint);color:var(--black);}
.cell--rust{background:var(--rust);color:var(--paper);}
.cell--lacquer{background:var(--lacquer);color:var(--paper);}

.g12{grid-template-columns:repeat(12,1fr);}
@media (max-width:1199px){
  .g12{grid-template-columns:repeat(6,1fr);}
}
@media (max-width:767px){
  .g12{grid-template-columns:1fr;}
  .g12 > *{grid-column:1 / -1 !important;}
}

.c-2{grid-column:span 2;}
.c-3{grid-column:span 3;}
.c-4{grid-column:span 4;}
.c-5{grid-column:span 5;}
.c-6{grid-column:span 6;}
.c-7{grid-column:span 7;}
.c-8{grid-column:span 8;}
.c-12{grid-column:span 12;}
@media (max-width:1199px){
  .c-7,.c-5,.c-8,.c-4{grid-column:span 6;}
}

.headline-50{font-size:var(--headline-50);line-height:.8;letter-spacing:-.04em;font-weight:500;}
.headline-40{font-size:var(--headline-40);line-height:1;letter-spacing:-.04em;font-weight:500;}
.headline-20{font-size:var(--headline-20);line-height:1;letter-spacing:-.04em;font-weight:500;}
.h3{font-size:var(--h3);line-height:1.1;letter-spacing:-.02em;font-weight:500;}
.body{font-size:var(--body);line-height:1.3;letter-spacing:-.02em;}
.body-30{font-size:var(--body-30);line-height:1.1;letter-spacing:-.02em;}
.caption{font-size:var(--caption);letter-spacing:0;}
.tnum{font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums;}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------- topline */
.topline{
  position:sticky;top:0;z-index:40;height:48px;max-width:1440px;margin:0 auto;
  display:grid;grid-template-columns:auto 1fr auto;gap:1px;background:#000;
}
.topline-cell{background:var(--black);color:var(--paper);display:flex;align-items:center;padding:0 20px;}
.topline-logo{width:auto;height:22px;}
.topline-mark{font-size:15px;letter-spacing:-.02em;font-weight:500;}
.topline-mid{background:var(--paper);}
.topline-contact{background:var(--black);color:var(--paper);font-size:14px;text-decoration:none;justify-content:flex-end;}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------- hero */
/* R3: the fixed 190svh CSS-sticky stage is gone. The pin distance is now
   owned by ScrollTrigger's own pinSpacing (desktop matchMedia branch,
   RORELSE-SPEC.md §2); hero-wrap just needs to size to its content so a
   no-JS/pre-JS view still shows one full stage, not a dead 90svh gap. */
.hero-wrap{position:relative;max-width:1440px;margin:0 auto;}
.hero-stage{
  position:relative;height:calc(100svh - 48px);
  display:grid;grid-template-columns:1fr 1fr;grid-template-rows:1fr 1fr;
  gap:1px;background:#000;
}
@media (max-width:767px){
  /* Mobile drops the pin: no extra scroll-span, no sticky stage. The four
     cells stack in normal flow (each already min-height:60vw, so the
     stack is naturally taller than one screen) and the card flips against
     that natural scroll distance instead of a dedicated dead-space span. */
  .hero-wrap{height:auto;}
  .hero-stage{grid-template-columns:1fr;grid-template-rows:repeat(4,minmax(60vw,auto));height:auto;position:relative;top:0;}
}
.hero-cell{position:relative;overflow:hidden;}
.hero-ov{background:var(--paper);display:flex;align-items:flex-end;padding:var(--cellpad);}
.hero-oh{background:var(--grey);}
.hero-nv{background:var(--grey);}
.hero-nh{background:var(--mint);}
.hero-h1{max-width:14ch;}

.dither-layer{position:absolute;inset:0;width:100%;height:100%;object-fit:cover;}
.color-layer{position:absolute;inset:0;width:100%;height:100%;object-fit:cover;}

/* card: a physical object (light stock, ink edge, hard offset shadow) so
   it reads against a black cell instead of disappearing into it. ~1.6x
   the R1 size at 1440 (was ~340px wide, now ~520px), 85:55 kept. */
.card-anchor{
  position:absolute;left:75%;top:50%;
  width:min(36vw,520px);
  aspect-ratio:85/55;
  transform:translate(-50%,-50%);
  perspective:1600px;
  z-index:5;
  pointer-events:none;
}
@media (max-width:767px){ .card-anchor{left:50%;top:120vw;width:min(74vw,380px);} }
.card-flip{
  width:100%;height:100%;position:relative;
  transform-style:preserve-3d;
  transform:rotateY(calc(var(--flip,0) * 180deg));
  box-shadow:10px 10px 0 0 #000;
}
.face{
  position:absolute;inset:0;
  background:#fff;
  backface-visibility:hidden;
  border:1px solid #000;
  overflow:hidden;
}
/* A visible white mat around the photo, not a full-bleed image: a card
   that is a photo edge-to-edge reads as "the photo", not as "a light
   stock object sitting on the cell" - the mat is what makes the white
   stock actually visible against a black ÖH ground. */
.face--front{background:#fff;padding:6%;}
/* R6 bugfix: kontakt's front is a <button> wrapping <span>s (spans, unlike
   hero's <div>s, default to display:inline) - an inline, merely
   position:relative .photo never gets a real box (width/height are ignored
   on non-replaced inline elements), so it collapsed to a ~2px sliver and
   the absolutely-positioned img inside inherited that zero-size containing
   block. display:block here makes both tags behave identically. */
.face--front .photo{display:block;position:relative;width:100%;height:100%;overflow:hidden;border:1px solid rgba(0,0,0,.5);}
.face--back{
  transform:rotateY(180deg);
  background:#fff;color:var(--ink);
  display:flex;flex-direction:column;justify-content:center;gap:10px;padding:6% 8%;
}
.face--front img{position:absolute;inset:0;width:100%;height:100%;object-fit:cover;}
.mark-dock{position:absolute;top:9%;left:9%;width:14%;z-index:2;}
.mark-dock svg{width:100%;height:auto;fill:#fff;filter:drop-shadow(0 0 3px rgba(0,0,0,.7));}
.card-mark{font-size:clamp(20px,2.6vw,32px);letter-spacing:-.02em;margin:0;}
.card-kicker{font-family:"Geist Mono";font-weight:400;font-size:clamp(11px,1.1vw,14px);opacity:.65;margin:2px 0 0;}
.card-rule{border:0;border-top:1px solid rgba(0,0,0,.25);margin:6px 0;width:100%;}
.card-services{display:flex;gap:10px;font-family:"Geist Mono";font-weight:400;font-size:clamp(10px,1.1vw,13px);}
.card-cta{font-size:clamp(13px,1.5vw,18px);text-decoration:underline;margin-top:4px;}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------- tes */
.tes-top{background:var(--black);color:var(--paper);padding:calc(var(--cellpad)*2) var(--cellpad);}
.tes-top .headline-50{max-width:22ch;}
.tes-lower{min-height:104svh;}
.tes-stack{display:grid;grid-template-rows:repeat(3,1fr);gap:1px;background:#000;}
.tes-line{padding:var(--cellpad);display:flex;align-items:center;}
.tes-image{padding:0;}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------- process */
.process-row{}
.process-left{background:var(--grey);}
.process-sticky{position:sticky;top:calc(48px + var(--cellpad));}
.process-kicker{margin-bottom:14px;}
.process-title{margin:0 0 18px;max-width:11ch;}
.process-lock{max-width:32ch;opacity:.8;}
.process-image{position:relative;margin-top:32px;aspect-ratio:1/1;width:100%;max-width:680px;border:1px solid #000;overflow:hidden;}
.process-right{background:var(--black);color:var(--paper);padding:0;}
.process-steps{list-style:none;}
.process-row-item{display:grid;grid-template-columns:56px 1fr;gap:14px;padding:22px var(--cellpad);border-top:1px solid #000;}
.process-row-item:first-child{border-top:none;}
.process-num{font-family:"Geist Mono";font-weight:400;font-size:13px;padding-top:4px;}
.process-step-title{margin:0 0 6px;}
.process-p{color:#bdbdbd;max-width:56ch;font-size:15px;}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------- exempelcase */
/* R5 §A bugfix: 0.6x bottom padding (12px) was less than the SplitText
   mask-breathe allowance (0.16em, ~16-20px at this clamp size) needs to
   clear the word's own descenders before the cell's overflow:hidden edge
   - verify_motion.py's legibility scan caught the word's rendered box
   (with its mask wrapper's padding-bottom) genuinely sitting a few px
   below the cell's clip boundary at every scroll position (0vh visible,
   not >=40vh). Matching the top padding removes the clip entirely. */
.case-word-cell{padding:calc(var(--cellpad)*1.4) var(--cellpad) calc(var(--cellpad)*1.4 + 4px);overflow:hidden;}
.case-word-cell .headline-50{max-width:100%;}

/* R5 §B1: väljaren - två knappar, skarpa 1440x900-vyer, ingen beskärande zoom */
.case-picker-cell{padding:0 var(--cellpad) calc(var(--cellpad)*1.2);background:#000;}
.case-picker{display:grid;gap:1px;background:#000;}
.case-choice{
  display:block;width:100%;margin:0;padding:0;border:0;background:var(--paper);color:inherit;
  font:inherit;text-align:left;cursor:pointer;-webkit-appearance:none;appearance:none;
}
.case-choice-frame{position:relative;display:block;aspect-ratio:16/10;overflow:hidden;background:var(--grey);}
.case-choice-frame img{position:absolute;inset:0;width:100%;height:100%;object-fit:cover;transform:scale(1);transition:transform .7s cubic-bezier(.23,1,.32,1);will-change:transform;}
@media (hover:hover){
  .case-choice:hover .case-choice-frame img,
  .case-choice:focus-visible .case-choice-frame img{transform:scale(1.04);}
}
.case-choice:focus-visible{outline:2px solid var(--mint);outline-offset:-2px;}
.case-choice-meta{display:block;padding:16px var(--cellpad) 20px;border-bottom:4px solid transparent;}
.case-choice[aria-pressed="true"] .case-choice-meta{border-bottom-color:var(--mint);}
.case-choice-meta .h3{display:block;margin-bottom:4px;font-size:22px;}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------- showcase (B2/C) */
.showcase-stage{display:grid;grid-template-columns:1fr;gap:1px;background:#000;}
@media (min-width:768px){ .showcase-stage{grid-template-columns:7fr 5fr;} }
.showcase-embed-cell{padding:0;background:var(--paper);position:relative;overflow:hidden;}
.showcase-embed-cell .showcase-frame-wrap{position:relative;width:100%;height:100%;overflow:hidden;background:var(--paper);}
.showcase-embed-cell .showcase-poster{position:absolute;inset:0;width:100%;height:100%;object-fit:cover;}
.showcase-embed-cell iframe{
  position:absolute;top:0;left:0;width:1440px;height:900px;border:0;background:var(--paper);
  transform-origin:top left;pointer-events:none;opacity:0;
}
@media (max-width:767px){
  .showcase-embed-cell{position:sticky;top:48px;height:56svh;z-index:2;}
}
@media (min-width:768px){
  /* R6 §3, two stacked causes, both fixed here:
     1) .showcase-side's natural content (all 5/6 rows, R5's rise-mask kept
        every body visible at once) was taller than the embed cell's
        explicit height. A CSS grid item with an explicit height does not
        stretch to match a taller sibling's row track - the TRACK grows to
        fit the tall side instead, leaving the embed cell short of the
        row's actual height by the difference (measured ~110px), exposing
        the stage's own black gap background below the frame. Pinning both
        columns to the SAME explicit height (with the side's own
        overflow-y:auto as a never-clip safety net) makes them structurally
        impossible to mismatch, regardless of how much text a future edit
        adds.
     2) That explicit height was `100svh - 48px`, sized to sit BELOW the
        48px sticky topline - but the pin (`start:'top top'`) puts the
        section's rendered top at the viewport's own y:0, with the topline
        merely painted on top of (not offsetting) its first 48px. The
        result: content correctly avoids the topline visually, but then
        runs 48px short of the viewport's bottom edge, showing the stage's
        black background as a trailing band under both columns (measured:
        embed/side bottom at 852 of a 900-tall viewport). Hero's own pin
        has this identical 48px arithmetic and gap - invisible there only
        because it lands on the page's own black background either side.
        Showcase's is visible because there's real content flush above it.
        Fixed the same way hero's is invisible: fill the FULL viewport
        (100svh) - the topline still visually covers the top 48px (it's
        position:sticky, z-index:40, opaque), but the bottom now lands
        exactly on the viewport edge, so no gap is left to expose.

     R7 runda 2, fynd 1: that "topline merely painted on top" claim was
     wrong for `.showcase-head`'s own rubrik - the topline IS opaque and
     DOES cover whatever renders in its first 48px; it just happened not to
     matter for hero (dark ground either side). Here `.showcase-head`'s
     headline-40 sits flush at the pinned section's very top edge, so its
     cap-height rendered UNDER the topline and got visually sheared (lead's
     through-05..through-12, 2026-09-25). Fix: pin the section 48px lower
     instead of hiding 48px under an opaque bar - `start:'top top+=48'` on
     the ScrollTrigger (setupDesktopEngine) puts the section's rendered top
     at y:48, exactly below the topline, and both cell heights shrink by
     the same 48px so the bottom still lands flush on the viewport edge -
     the R6 §3 gap this block fixed doesn't reopen, because now BOTH the
     offset and the height account for the topline, not just the height. */
  .showcase-embed-cell{height:calc(100svh - 48px);}
  .showcase-side{height:calc(100svh - 48px);overflow-y:auto;}
}
.showcase-side{display:grid;grid-template-rows:auto 1fr;gap:1px;background:#000;}
.showcase-panel{display:contents;}
.showcase-head{padding:calc(var(--cellpad)*1.4) var(--cellpad);}
.showcase-head .headline-40{margin-bottom:8px;}

/* R7 §C: the accordion ledger (R6 §1/§2) is replaced on desktop by a single
   crossfading box - one background for the whole "ruta", every step
   grid-stacked in one cell and GSAP-scrubbed by the showcase pin's onUpdate
   (never a class-toggle). Mobile keeps R6's stacked-rows layout unchanged;
   only its opacity mechanism changes (measured contrast fix, see below). */
.showcase-row{padding:var(--cellpad);display:flex;flex-direction:column;justify-content:center;}
.showcase-row h3{margin-bottom:0;}
.showcase-row p{max-width:52ch;font-size:15px;margin-top:8px;}

@media (min-width:768px){
  /* R6 runda 6 (F-019/F-022): tre celler i sidans eget rutverk (gap:1px,
     background:#000 skiner igenom som fog, varje cell sin egen bakgrund) -
     räknarcellen (auto), textcellen (auto, satt av det längsta stegets
     höjd via samma grid-area:1/1-stapling som förut) och en ny detaljcell
     (1fr, fyller resten) som visar en bild ur den valda sajten per steg.
     Den lodräta stegskalan (R3-R4) är borttagen helt - Anton (F-022):
     "Det ser ut som något ofärdigt". Tom yta löses nu med riktigt innehåll
     (en bild ur arbetet), inte med ett dekorativt streck. */
  .showcase-rows{display:grid;grid-template-rows:auto auto 1fr;gap:1px;background:#000;height:100%;}
  .showcase-panel--calyx .showcase-box-head,
  .showcase-panel--calyx .showcase-steps{background:var(--paper);color:var(--ink);}
  .showcase-panel--horai .showcase-box-head,
  .showcase-panel--horai .showcase-steps{background:var(--black);color:var(--paper);}
  .showcase-panel--horai .showcase-row p{color:#bdbdbd;}
  /* räknarcellen: NN/NN överst, mintspåret under - som R3, innan R4 flyttade
     räknaren ned i den nu borttagna skalan. */
  .showcase-box-head{padding:var(--cellpad);}
  .showcase-counter{display:block;font-size:13px;margin-bottom:10px;}
  .showcase-track{position:relative;height:4px;}
  .showcase-track::before{content:'';position:absolute;top:50%;left:0;right:0;height:1px;background:#000;transform:translateY(-50%);}
  .showcase-panel--horai .showcase-track::before{background:var(--paper);opacity:.3;}
  .showcase-track-fill{position:absolute;top:0;left:0;width:100%;height:4px;background:var(--mint);transform-origin:0 50%;transform:scaleX(0);}
  .showcase-steps{display:grid;}
  /* R3 §4 (F-019): rubriken får aldrig ta över - sajten är huvudsaken,
     rutan är bildtexten. h3 tillbaka i rubrikskala (30px), inte
     headline-40-tokenet R2 lånade; jättesiffran är borttagen. */
  /* R6b: toppjusterad. Centrerad (basregeln) satte stegrubriken 14 px lägre i
     steg med tre rader än i steg med fyra, så rubriken hoppade vid varje byte. */
  .showcase-row{grid-area:1/1;padding:0 var(--cellpad) calc(var(--cellpad)*1.4);justify-content:flex-start;}
  .showcase-row h3{font-size:30px;line-height:1.15;font-weight:500;}
  .showcase-row p{font-size:18px;line-height:1.5;max-width:40ch;}
  /* detaljcellen: en <figure> per steg, grid-stackad (samma grid-area:1/1-
     teknik som .showcase-row ovan), färglager under och ett dither-rutnät
     ovanpå (buildTileGrid, samma mekanism som #kontakt/tes-bilden) som
     löses upp i den skrubbade pin-tidslinjen (C.tl, se buildStepTimelines).
     Calyx grå grund (dither svart-på-grått), Hōrai svart grund (dither
     vitt-på-svart) - samma två grundfärger dither.py redan producerar. */
  /* R6b: bilden är ett förstoringsglas (2,5-3x iframen) tagen i exakt cellens
     proportion vid 1440x900 (599,6/426,5 = 1,4058). Vid andra fönster varierar
     cellen från 0,63 (2560x1440) till 1,59 (1280x800); figuren låses därför
     till bildens proportion och passas in (contain) med container-enheter, så
     att färglagret och rutnätet ovanpå alltid täcker samma yta. Med cover
     klipptes luppen (adressen, priset) och rutorna gled ur linje mot färgen. */
  .showcase-detail{position:relative;overflow:hidden;min-height:0;container-type:size;}
  .showcase-panel--calyx .showcase-detail{background:var(--grey);}
  .showcase-panel--horai .showcase-detail{background:var(--black);}
  .showcase-figure{position:absolute;left:50%;top:50%;translate:-50% -50%;width:min(100cqw,140.58cqh);height:min(100cqh,71.13cqw);margin:0;opacity:0;}
  .showcase-figure:first-child{opacity:1;}
  .showcase-figure img{position:absolute;inset:0;width:100%;height:100%;object-fit:fill;}
}
@media (max-width:767px){
  /* R7 runda 2, fynd 2: .showcase-embed-cell (position:sticky) satt över
     .showcase-side (head + rader) i normalt dokumentflöde, så när huvudet
     ("Hōrai") rullade upp genom den redan-klistrade ramen (z-index:2) klipptes
     det mot ramens underkant (lead: through-02/03). Huvudet ska stå helt
     synligt INNAN raderna - och innan ramen - börjar klistra, så .showcase-side
     görs display:contents här (bara mobil) för att lyfta .showcase-head och
     .showcase-rows till .showcase-stage's egna grid-items, och ordnas om med
     `order`: huvud (1) -> ram (2, där klistringen börjar) -> rader (3). */
  .showcase-side{display:contents;}
  .showcase-head{order:1;}
  .showcase-embed-cell{order:2;}
  .showcase-rows{display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:1px;background:#000;order:3;}
  /* R6 runda 6: .showcase-box-head hålls INTE display:none längre. Mätt
     (shots/r6-mobile-before, före denna runda): den borttagna stegskalan
     (.showcase-scale) hade ALDRIG en egen mobilregel, så dess räknartext
     redan föll igenom osynligt formaterad, som en enkel textrad i
     .showcase-rows egen svarta gap-bakgrund, ovanpå .showcase-embed-cell.
     Räknaren (nu flyttad hit) måste fortsätta synas EXAKT så - briefen
     ("mobil oförändrad") gäller även denna oavsiktliga men redan existerande
     synlighet. .showcase-track har fortfarande ingen mobilstorlek (dess
     height/position-regler ligger kvar i 768px-blocket ovan) och kollapsar
     därför osynligt till 0px, precis som förut. */
  .showcase-detail{display:none;}
  .showcase-steps{display:contents;}
  .showcase-panel--calyx .showcase-row:nth-child(odd){background:var(--paper);}
  .showcase-panel--calyx .showcase-row:nth-child(even){background:var(--grey);}
  .showcase-panel--horai .showcase-row:nth-child(odd){background:var(--black);color:var(--paper);}
  .showcase-panel--horai .showcase-row:nth-child(odd) p{color:#bdbdbd;}
  .showcase-panel--horai .showcase-row:nth-child(even){background:var(--grey);}
}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------- pris */
.pris-statement{padding:calc(var(--cellpad)*2) var(--cellpad);}
.pris-statement .body-30{max-width:60ch;margin-top:16px;font-weight:500;}
/* All placement lives in these classes (not inline styles) so the media
   queries below can actually win the cascade at each breakpoint. */
.pris-bento{grid-template-columns:repeat(12,1fr);grid-template-rows:auto auto;}
.pris-lead{grid-column:1 / span 6;grid-row:1 / span 2;background:var(--mint);display:flex;flex-direction:column;justify-content:space-between;gap:24px;}
.pris-tier{display:flex;flex-direction:column;justify-content:space-between;gap:18px;min-height:220px;}
.pris-tier-a{grid-column:7 / span 6;grid-row:1;background:var(--paper);}
.pris-tier-b{grid-column:7 / span 6;grid-row:2;background:var(--grey);}
@media (max-width:1199px){
  .pris-bento{grid-template-columns:1fr 1fr;}
  .pris-lead{grid-column:1 / span 2;grid-row:1;}
  .pris-tier-a{grid-column:1;grid-row:2;}
  .pris-tier-b{grid-column:2;grid-row:2;}
}
@media (max-width:767px){
  .pris-bento{grid-template-columns:1fr;}
  .pris-lead,.pris-tier-a,.pris-tier-b{grid-column:1;grid-row:auto;min-height:0;}
}
.price-label{max-width:34ch;font-size:15px;}
.price-value{font-size:clamp(28px,3.6vw,44px);letter-spacing:-.03em;}
.price-value .unit{font-size:.5em;margin-left:2px;}
.price-value--text{font-size:clamp(18px,2vw,24px);}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------- kontakt (R5 §C: heron speglad) */
.kontakt-quad{
  position:relative;display:grid;gap:1px;background:#000;min-height:100svh;
  grid-template-columns:1fr 1fr;grid-template-rows:1fr 1fr;
  grid-template-areas:"ov oh" "nv nh";
}
.kontakt-q{position:relative;overflow:hidden;padding:var(--cellpad);}
.kontakt-q--ov{grid-area:ov;background:var(--black);color:var(--paper);display:flex;flex-direction:column;justify-content:flex-end;gap:10px;}
/* R6 §4: headline-40 is tuned for a single "jätteord" (hero, case names) -
   at this cell's half-page width, a four-word sentence in it ran past the
   ÖV/ÖH seam (measured x>720 at 1440, into the card's own space). A
   smaller, dedicated clamp - same family as the old kontakt-giant's - fits
   three lines comfortably inside the cell at 1440/1280/768, verified with
   getBoundingClientRect against the cell box, not eyeballed. */
.kontakt-q--ov h2{
  font-size:clamp(1.75rem, 1.1rem + 2.6vw, 3.4rem);line-height:1.05;
  letter-spacing:-.03em;font-weight:500;max-width:12ch;
}
.kontakt-q--ov p{max-width:32ch;font-size:15px;}
.kontakt-q--oh{grid-area:oh;background:var(--paper);}
.kontakt-q--nv{grid-area:nv;background:var(--grey);padding:0;}
.kontakt-q--nh{grid-area:nh;background:var(--mint);}
@media (max-width:767px){
  /* R6 §7: nh gets more room than ov/nv (was the same minmax(60vw) as
     both) - a 3D Y-axis rotation's perspective projection genuinely bulges
     a flat card's rendered bounding box taller at the near edge as it
     turns (measured: +/-28px top/bottom at 1200px perspective, still
     +/-24px at 3000px - foreshortening a rotated rectangle really does
     grow its axis-aligned bbox, not a rounding artefact), and centring an
     88%-wide card in a 60vw-tall row left only ~27px clearance to the
     subline above - not enough to survive that bulge at any angle in the
     0-180deg sweep. */
  .kontakt-quad{grid-template-columns:1fr;grid-template-rows:minmax(60vw,auto) minmax(76vw,auto) minmax(60vw,auto);grid-template-areas:"ov" "nh" "nv";min-height:auto;}
  .kontakt-q--oh{display:none;}
}

/* the card sits on the crossing of all four quadrants (a grid item that
   spans the full 2x2 and centres itself), mirroring heron's own card. On
   mobile it drops into the mint cell's own grid area instead, 88% wide. */
/* R6 §4/§7: centred on the FULL 2x2 crossing put the card's top edge only
   ~15-50px below the headline row at rest, with zero margin for the flip's
   lift or the hover-tilt's foreshortening - both could (and did, measured)
   bring the card within single-digit px of "verksamhet.". Spanning only
   the LOWER row (grid-row:2, still centred horizontally on the vertical
   seam = still "on the crossing") puts the card inside the NV/NH half
   entirely, with a full row-height of clearance above it before ÖV even
   starts. */
.kontakt-card-anchor{
  grid-column:1 / 3;grid-row:2;place-self:center;z-index:5;
  width:min(32vw,460px);aspect-ratio:85/55;perspective:1200px;
}
@media (max-width:767px){
  .kontakt-card-anchor{grid-area:nh;place-self:center;width:80%;}
}
.kontakt-card-tilt{width:100%;height:100%;position:relative;transform-style:preserve-3d;}
.card-flip2{width:100%;height:100%;position:relative;transform-style:preserve-3d;box-shadow:10px 10px 0 0 #000;}
.card-flip2 button.face{margin:0;padding:6%;font:inherit;text-align:left;cursor:pointer;display:block;width:100%;height:100%;}
.card-flip2 button.face:focus-visible{outline:2px solid var(--mint);outline-offset:2px;}
.face-back-hit{position:absolute;inset:0;z-index:0;background:transparent;border:0;padding:0;margin:0;cursor:pointer;}
.face-back-hit:focus-visible{outline:2px solid var(--mint);outline-offset:2px;}
.card-back-content{position:relative;z-index:1;height:100%;display:flex;flex-direction:column;justify-content:center;gap:10px;pointer-events:none;}
.card-back-content a{pointer-events:auto;}
.card-back-links{display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:6px;margin-top:4px;}
.card-back-links a{font-size:clamp(13px,1.5vw,18px);text-decoration:underline;width:max-content;}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------- footer */
.footer-cell{background:var(--black);color:var(--paper);padding:0 0 0 var(--cellpad);height:34vw;max-height:340px;min-height:200px;display:flex;align-items:flex-end;overflow:hidden;}
.footer-mark{font-size:clamp(80px,16vw,220px);line-height:.8;letter-spacing:-.04em;white-space:nowrap;padding-bottom:.06em;}
.footer-strip{padding:18px var(--cellpad);background:var(--black);color:var(--paper);}
.footer-strip a{text-decoration:underline;font-size:14px;}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------- resolve (dither -> color) */
.img-cell{position:relative;}
/* R3: §3 dither -> colour grid-stagger. The tile grid sits over the
   already-visible colour layer; each tile shows one slice of the dither
   image and fades on its own random-order schedule, so the resolve reads
   as pixels dissolving away rather than a wipe. Built once at init from
   the existing .dither-layer <img> (see buildTileGrid in the script). */
.tile-grid{position:absolute;inset:0;display:grid;pointer-events:none;}
.tile-grid > span{display:block;background-repeat:no-repeat;will-change:opacity;}
.color-layer{clip-path:none;}

/* R3: seam-anchored decorations, all created/positioned by the script. */
.seam-line{position:absolute;background:var(--mint);pointer-events:none;z-index:3;}
/* the crosshair seam-draw is a 2x2-grid flourish; hero-stage stacks to one
   column under 768px (see .hero-stage media query above), so the same
   absolute-positioned lines would otherwise bisect the whole stacked
   column top to bottom - hide them there. */
@media (max-width:767px){ .seam-line{display:none;} }
.process-row{position:relative;}
.process-progress{position:absolute;top:0;bottom:0;width:2px;background:var(--mint);transform:scaleY(0);transform-origin:top center;pointer-events:none;z-index:6;}
/* process-left/process-right only sit side by side at the 1200px+ 12-col
   grid (BYGGSPEC .g12 breakpoints); below that they stack, so the seam
   the progress line marks no longer exists - hide it rather than let a
   stale left-offset poke 2px past the right edge (390/768 overflow). */
@media (max-width:1199px){ .process-progress{display:none;} }

/* R3: SplitText's own mask:'lines'/'words'/'chars' option wraps each split
   unit in its own clipping span, and every heading that gets split already
   sits inside a .cell (overflow:hidden) or .footer-cell (overflow:hidden)
   — so no extra clip rule is needed on the headings themselves (adding one
   risked cutting descenders that round 2's static layout already relies
   on fitting without it). */

/* spacing rhythm between section groups */
.rhythm{height:110px;}
@media (max-width:767px){ .rhythm{height:72px;} }
</style>
</head>

commands.name: foreman:ai-augmentation-not-automation
commands.description: (foreman) Makes the strategic and moral case for AI augmentation over pure automation, providing leaders with frameworks for job redesign, creativity-driven AI deployment, and long-term workforce investment. Draws on the centaur model from chess and case studies across industries to demonstrate that human-AI collaboration outperforms either alone. Use when deciding between automating jobs and redesigning them, when AI adoption is eroding workforce skills, when boards pressure for automation-driven cost cuts, when designing new roles that pair human creativity with AI capabilities, or when facing the long-term consequences of over-automation.

commands.name: foreman:ai-communication-culture
commands.description: (foreman) Equips leaders to build flat, participative communication cultures that enable successful AI adoption by bridging technical and business teams, democratising data, and establishing feedback loops. Covers the symphony conductor model, soliciting expert feedback, removing bureaucratic obstacles, and building shared responsibility. Use when AI projects fail due to communication breakdowns, when data scientists and business leaders operate in silos, when employees lack channels to provide AI feedback, when hierarchical structures block information flow, or when leaders need to translate between technical and business perspectives.

commands.name: foreman:ai-emotional-intelligence
commands.description: (foreman) Argues that emotional intelligence becomes strategically critical precisely because of AI -- not despite it -- and provides leaders with practices for developing the soft skills that constitute the human competitive advantage in an AI-saturated economy. Covers empathy, self-awareness, communication beyond technical details, curiosity, proactive problem-solving, trust-building through vulnerability, and coaching teams in EI. Use when an AI project is failing due to poor leadership connection, when technical leaders cannot engage the workforce emotionally, when employees feel reduced to data points, when building the case for soft skills investment alongside AI investment, or when developing the human capabilities that AI cannot replicate.

commands.name: foreman:ai-era-leadership
commands.description: (foreman) Prepares leaders for daily effectiveness in an AI-augmented workplace by focusing on the human capabilities that machines cannot replicate. Covers five irreplaceable leadership skills (interpersonal intelligence, analog relationship-building, creative unpredictability, domain credibility, and preskilling), practical routines for leading hybrid human-AI teams, and strategies for staying relevant as automation reshapes every function. Use when planning workforce development around AI adoption, when leaders feel threatened by automation, when building AI-human collaboration norms, or when advising on career resilience in technology-disrupted industries.

commands.name: foreman:ai-human-centered-approach
commands.description: (foreman) Provides a comprehensive framework for deploying AI in ways that respect employee psychology, preserve human agency, and treat workforce well-being as a strategic priority rather than an afterthought. Addresses the hidden fears employees harbour about AI, the psychological damage of algorithmic supervision, and the practical steps for making human needs central to technology decisions. Use when employees resist AI adoption, when algorithmic monitoring is eroding morale, when AI-driven productivity targets create burnout, when planning an AI rollout that affects frontline workers, or when an AI project is failing and the technology is not the problem.

commands.name: foreman:ai-inclusive-collaboration
commands.description: (foreman) Provides a comprehensive framework for designing inclusive human-AI collaboration that keeps all stakeholders at the design table. Addresses exclusion dynamics, algorithm aversion, trust deficits, silo formation, and the human cost of automation-first strategies. Use when employees resist AI adoption, when AI design excludes non-technical voices, when human-AI collaboration feels extractive rather than empowering, when organisational silos hinder AI scaling, or when leaders need to reward human contributions in AI-augmented work.

commands.name: foreman:ai-learning-for-leaders
commands.description: (foreman) Guides non-technical leaders through building AI savviness without becoming AI experts, closing the gap between AI understanding and AI deployment. Applies the 'just savvy enough' principle and lifelong AI learning framework. Use when a leader feels inadequate about AI knowledge, defers too heavily to technologists, needs to build a business case for AI, wants to lead AI adoption without a technical background, or seeks to distinguish AI-knowledgeable from AI-savvy leadership.

commands.name: foreman:ai-purpose-driven-questions
commands.description: (foreman) Teaches leaders to ground AI adoption in organisational purpose by asking the right questions before selecting tools. Applies the purpose-driven framework to prevent technology-for-technology's-sake deployments. Use when evaluating AI investments against business goals, when data scientists operate without strategic direction, when AI projects lack clear problem definitions, when aligning AI initiatives with company values, or when leaders are tempted to adopt AI because competitors have.

commands.name: foreman:ai-stakeholder-balance
commands.description: (foreman) Guides leaders through the ethical and strategic complexities of balancing multiple stakeholder interests during AI adoption, from employees and customers to society at large. Provides frameworks for responsible AI deployment, stakeholder impact mapping, and moral decision-making when efficiency gains conflict with human welfare. Use when evaluating whether an AI deployment will harm employees or customers, weighing automation against workforce impact, facing pressure to prioritise shareholders over other stakeholders, designing an AI ethics governance structure, or confronting the societal consequences of algorithmic decision-making.

commands.name: foreman:ai-vision-and-strategy
commands.description: (foreman) Guides leaders in developing and communicating a compelling AI vision that inspires rather than threatens, choosing augmentation over replacement as the strategic paradigm. Covers Perspective 1 (AI replaces humans) vs. Perspective 2 (AI augments humans), the tech-driving-tech trap, holistic communication, ethical foresight, and agile visionary leadership. Use when setting long-term AI strategy, when employees fear AI will eliminate their jobs, when AI adoption lacks a unifying narrative, when vision statements betray organisational identity, or when leaders need to translate AI potential into a story that builds commitment.

commands.name: foreman:ambidexterity
commands.description: (foreman) Applies O'Reilly and Tushman's organizational ambidexterity framework to balance exploitation of existing business with exploration of new opportunities. Assesses resource allocation between core operations and innovation initiatives, designs structurally or contextually ambidextrous organizations, and evaluates innovation portfolios. Use when a company needs to protect its core revenue while pursuing new growth, launching separate innovation units, or diagnosing why exploratory initiatives are being starved by day-to-day operations.

commands.name: foreman:appreciative-inquiry
commands.description: (foreman) Guides strengths-based organizational change using Cooperrider's Appreciative Inquiry 4D cycle: Discovery, Dream, Design, and Delivery. Surfaces peak experiences and positive patterns to amplify what works rather than fixing what is broken. Use when addressing team morale, redesigning processes, integrating acquisitions, reframing organizational challenges, or running culture transformation initiatives where traditional deficit-based problem-solving has stalled.

commands.name: foreman:art-of-war
commands.description: (foreman) Applies Sun Tzu's strategic principles to competitive business situations, covering self-knowledge and competitor intelligence, winning without direct confrontation, speed and timing, terrain analysis, and strategic positioning. Use when assessing competitive landscapes, developing market entry strategies, evaluating when to fight or avoid competitors, conducting competitive intelligence audits, or designing stealth positioning for startups facing well-resourced incumbents.

commands.name: foreman:balanced-scorecard
commands.description: (foreman) Builds and evaluates Kaplan and Norton's Balanced Scorecard across four perspectives: Financial, Customer, Internal Process, and Learning and Growth. Creates strategy maps linking causal chains from learning investments through process improvements to customer outcomes and financial results. Use when designing KPI systems, aligning teams around strategy, diagnosing why financial metrics are lagging, auditing measurement balance, or establishing leading indicators for organizational health.

commands.name: foreman:belbin-team-roles
commands.description: (foreman) Analyzes team composition using Belbin's nine team roles across Thinking, Action, and People categories. Maps team members to roles such as Plant, Shaper, Coordinator, Implementer, and others to identify gaps, overlaps, and imbalances. Use when hiring to fill role gaps, diagnosing recurring team conflicts, auditing founding team balance, resolving execution problems caused by missing behavioral profiles, or assessing board composition.

commands.name: foreman:black-swans
commands.description: (foreman) Applies Taleb's Black Swan theory to assess and mitigate exposure to rare, high-impact unpredictable events. Distinguishes between Mediocristan and Extremistan domains, designs barbell strategies, builds antifragility, and audits business vulnerabilities including supply chain concentration, customer dependency, and regulatory risk. Use when stress-testing a business model, evaluating tail risks, designing resilience architecture, or building robust strategies that survive shocks rather than attempting to predict them.

commands.name: foreman:blue-ocean-strategy
commands.description: (foreman) Applies Kim and Mauborgne's Blue Ocean Strategy to create uncontested market space through value innovation. Uses the Strategy Canvas to map competitive factors, the ERRC Grid to Eliminate-Reduce-Raise-Create value elements, and the Three Tiers of Noncustomers to identify untapped demand. Use when entering saturated markets, escaping price-based competition, redesigning a value proposition, identifying noncustomer segments, or evaluating whether a new venture creates a genuinely new market category.

commands.name: foreman:building-story-stakes
commands.description: (foreman) Teaches five named techniques for creating and sustaining narrative tension in any story. Applies when a founder needs to hold an audience's attention through a pitch, investor update, all-hands talk, or customer case study. Use when a narrative feels flat, when attention wanders mid-presentation, or when the storyteller senses the audience could walk away without consequence.

commands.name: foreman:building-thinking-strength
commands.description: (foreman) Develops the four internal muscles required for clear thinking -- self-accountability, self-knowledge, self-control, and self-confidence -- using the Clear Thinking strength-building system. Covers setting personal standards above external requirements, choosing exemplars, building a personal board of directors, and practising in sandboxes. Use when blaming external factors for poor outcomes, struggling to say no under social pressure, lacking the confidence to execute a difficult decision, noticing that team standards have drifted toward mediocrity, or seeking a structured approach to personal operating system design.

commands.name: foreman:business-model-canvas
commands.description: (foreman) Structures and evaluates business models using Osterwalder's nine-block Business Model Canvas: Customer Segments, Value Propositions, Channels, Customer Relationships, Revenue Streams, Key Resources, Key Activities, Key Partnerships, and Cost Structure. Use when designing a new venture, comparing business model alternatives, stress-testing assumptions, planning pivots, exploring revenue model options, or identifying hidden dependencies between business model components.

commands.name: foreman:business-writing-for-leaders
commands.description: (foreman) Sharpens leadership writing through four principles: write for the reader, lead with clarity, keep it simple, and sound human. Use when drafting company-wide announcements, writing investor updates, composing emails that require action, editing team communications for clarity, or noticing that written messages consistently generate confusion or non-response.

commands.name: foreman:career-strategy-for-leaders
commands.description: (foreman) Guides leaders through deliberate career design -- calculating timelines, auditing career fuel, breaking career-limiting habits, avoiding success traps, and aligning trade-offs with evolving values. Use when a leader feels stuck, faces a career crossroads, suspects their success has become a cage, needs to break a recurring bad habit, or wants to shift from reactive career drift to intentional career architecture.

commands.name: foreman:carnegie-win-friends
commands.description: (foreman) Applies Dale Carnegie's interpersonal influence principles for building relationships, earning trust, and leading without authority. Covers techniques for handling people, making others feel valued, winning people to your thinking, and changing behavior without giving offense. Use when building advisory networks, repairing strained stakeholder relationships, improving investor communications, navigating co-founder conflicts, or developing the interpersonal skills that underpin hiring, sales, and fundraising.

commands.name: foreman:choosing-and-executing
commands.description: (foreman) Provides a toolkit for moving from deliberation to commitment and from commitment to results. Covers the cost of decision paralysis, the 70% rule for when to stop gathering information, implementation planning after the choice is made, transparency as a trust mechanism, handling challenges to decisions, and combating second-guessing through process review rather than outcome regret. Use when stuck in analysis paralysis, when a decision has been made but needs implementation momentum, when stakeholders challenge or resist a decision, when second-guessing erodes confidence, or when building a decision communication plan.

commands.name: foreman:cialdini-influence
commands.description: (foreman) Applies Cialdini's seven principles of ethical persuasion -- Reciprocity, Commitment and Consistency, Social Proof, Authority, Liking, Scarcity, and Unity -- to business contexts including sales, marketing, fundraising, and negotiation. Use when designing conversion funnels, optimizing sales processes, preparing fundraising strategies, auditing marketing materials for persuasive effectiveness, planning negotiation tactics, or building community-driven growth while maintaining ethical boundaries.

commands.name: foreman:clarity-and-concision
commands.description: (foreman) Teaches techniques for achieving relentless clarity and ruthless concision in business writing, including the 20-word sentence rule, concrete detail over abstraction, word economy tactics, and the reader's perspective test. Features extensive before/after examples demonstrating how bloated corporate prose can be cut by 50-70% without losing meaning. Use when tightening any business document, eliminating wordiness, improving readability scores, preparing executive summaries, or when writing feels vague or overlong.

commands.name: foreman:coalition-and-partnership-games
commands.description: (foreman) Analyses partnership structures, cofounder equity splits, and alliance formation using coalitional game theory. Applies Shapley Value for contribution-based allocation, imputation sets and the core for stability testing, and coalition disintegration models to predict breakups. Use when splitting equity among cofounders, structuring joint ventures, negotiating alliance terms, evaluating vendor partnerships, diagnosing why a partnership is failing, or determining fair cost-sharing among unequal participants.

commands.name: foreman:competitive-negotiation
commands.description: (foreman) Executes the competitive negotiation process from opening move through final concession: anchoring strategy, ambitious asking, concession architecture, midpoint management, impasse-breaking through linkage, and closing discipline. Provides actionable protocols for value-claiming negotiations. Use when setting price in a sales negotiation, responding to an aggressive counter-offer, planning concession sequences for fundraising, structuring opening bids in acquisition talks, countering procurement hardball in enterprise deals, or coaching a sales team to stop discounting reflexively.

commands.name: foreman:connecting-with-people
commands.description: (foreman) Applies advanced interpersonal techniques for building genuine, lasting connections in entrepreneurial contexts. Covers the power of validation as the deepest form of listening, leading with 'How can I help you?' as a first-meeting strategy, maintaining authentic online identity, vulnerability as a professional strength, and the Platinum Rule that supersedes the Golden Rule by treating others as they want to be treated. Use when building investor relationships, resolving cofounder conflicts, designing customer-experience strategy, navigating cultural differences in international partnerships, or cultivating the authentic personal brand that underlies fundraising, hiring, and sales.

commands.name: foreman:cooperative-negotiation
commands.description: (foreman) Guides the practitioner through cooperative negotiation execution: transitioning from positions to interests, deploying empathy strategically, and following a structured six-step roadmap to resolution. Use when a competitive stance has stalled, when the relationship matters as much as the deal, when negotiating with a more powerful counterparty, when seeking creative value that positional bargaining cannot unlock, or when preparing for partnership, licensing, or joint-venture conversations.

commands.name: foreman:covey-seven-habits
commands.description: (foreman) Applies Stephen Covey's Seven Habits framework for personal and interpersonal effectiveness, progressing from dependence through independence to interdependence. Covers proactivity, mission clarity, prioritization, Win/Win thinking, empathic listening, synergy, and renewal. Use when conducting personal effectiveness audits, drafting mission statements, preparing Win/Win negotiations, resolving co-founder conflicts, designing founder renewal plans to prevent burnout, or building character-based leadership culture.

commands.name: foreman:creative-collaboration-and-context
commands.description: (foreman) Explores how creative collaboration produces outcomes neither party could achieve alone, covering reference points without copying, the role of creative mythology, the prism of self as competitive advantage, context as meaning-maker, cross-domain adaptation, and translation as a creative act. Use when building creative partnerships, navigating co-founder dynamics, assembling creative teams, repositioning a product through context change, adapting business models across industries, translating technical innovation for new markets, or understanding why the same idea succeeds in one context and fails in another.

commands.name: foreman:creative-completion-and-renewal
commands.description: (foreman) Addresses the hardest creative act -- finishing and releasing work -- covering the tension between experimenter and finisher mindsets, making choices when everything feels possible, accepting shades rather than absolutes, ending projects to begin anew, approaching new work with a clean slate, knowing when to stop refining, and recognising the energy living inside completed work. Use when struggling to ship a product, paralysed by perfectionism, unable to choose between competing directions, managing the transition between projects, deciding when a product version is ready for release, or recovering creative momentum after a major launch.

commands.name: foreman:creative-flow-and-inspiration
commands.description: (foreman) Teaches the experiential practice of courting creative inspiration, sustaining openness, creating conditions for breakthrough ideas, staying in creative mode continuously, harnessing spontaneity, practising connected detachment, and using play as a serious creative method. Use when seeking breakthrough product ideas, preparing for creative sessions, diagnosing why innovation has stalled, designing environments for creative teams, recovering creative energy after burnout, or cultivating the founder's capacity for original thinking under pressure.

commands.name: foreman:creative-identity-and-purpose
commands.description: (foreman) Applies the philosophy that creativity is a universal human capacity -- not a rare talent -- to help entrepreneurs reclaim their creative identity and redefine success on their own terms. Synthesises beginner's mind, the abundant mindset, non-competition, and creative freedom into a foundational framework for entrepreneurial self-expression. Use when doubting your creative ability, comparing yourself to competitors, trapped in scarcity thinking about ideas or market opportunity, struggling to define what success means for your venture, or needing permission to pursue an unconventional path.

commands.name: foreman:creative-obstacles
commands.description: (foreman) Addresses the internal resistances that derail entrepreneurial creativity -- self-doubt, distraction, undermining voices, the danger of expectations, and impatience -- using a contemplative creative framework. Provides strategies for navigating the inner critic, managing creative possession, and cultivating patience as a creative virtue. Use when paralysed by self-doubt about your venture, overwhelmed by internal or external criticism, struggling with perfectionism or unrealistic expectations, unable to distinguish productive obsession from destructive compulsion, or losing patience with the creative timeline of building a company.

commands.name: foreman:creative-perception-and-awareness
commands.description: (foreman) Develops the entrepreneur's capacity to receive creative signals by applying principles of tuning in, deep awareness, and perceptual sensitivity. Covers the vessel-and-filter model, seeing the unseen, nature as teacher, deep listening, the role of subconscious and memory, and how setting shapes creative output. Use when feeling creatively numb, missing market signals, unable to generate fresh product ideas, sensing that important information is passing you by, or needing to sharpen intuitive pattern recognition for innovation.

commands.name: foreman:creative-practice-and-habit
commands.description: (foreman) Transforms creativity from sporadic inspiration into daily discipline by applying principles of practice, habit formation, seed collection, experimentation, immersion in great works, and momentum management. Use when struggling to maintain a creative routine, waiting for inspiration to strike, unsure how to develop raw ideas into viable products, losing creative momentum mid-project, or wanting to improve the quality of creative inputs to elevate outputs.

commands.name: foreman:creative-shaping-and-craft
commands.description: (foreman) Guides the entrepreneur through shaping raw creative material into disciplined form, applying intention, rules, temporary constraints, assumption reversal, point-of-view discovery, pattern-breaking, and distillation to essence. Use when refining a product concept, setting creative direction for a brand, defining project constraints, challenging default assumptions about market or offering, finding a unique positioning voice, breaking creative stagnation, or stripping a pitch or product to its irreducible core.

commands.name: foreman:decision-making-under-pressure
commands.description: (foreman) Provides practical habits for making better decisions faster -- reframing problems before solving them, knowing when to stop deliberating, balancing intuition with analysis, resisting 'just this once' compromises, and breaking overthinking cycles. Use when facing a high-stakes choice with incomplete data, sensing that deliberation has become procrastination, noticing a pattern of deferred decisions, needing to explain decision-making rationale to a team, or recognising that overthinking is degrading output quality.

commands.name: foreman:decision-traps-and-roles
commands.description: (foreman) Catalogues the invisible psychological traps that sabotage decisions -- anchoring, sunk cost, confirming evidence, framing, and status quo bias -- and pairs them with the RAPID model for clarifying who recommends, agrees, performs, inputs, and decides, plus a seven-step checklist for faster group decisions. Use when a team suspects cognitive bias is distorting a choice, when decision authority is ambiguous, when past investments are influencing current strategy, when negotiations are anchored by the other party's opening, or when organisational decisions stall because no one knows who owns the call.

commands.name: foreman:defining-and-exploring-problems
commands.description: (foreman) Teaches the discipline of correct problem definition and structured solution exploration before any evaluation begins. Covers the problem-solution firewall, root cause identification, the premortem, second-order thinking ('and then what?'), binary thinking traps, integrative Both-And options, and opportunity cost analysis through the 3-Lens Principle. Use when a team is jumping to solutions before understanding the problem, when a founder suspects they are treating symptoms rather than causes, when only two options seem to exist, when opportunity costs are unclear, or when first-conclusion bias is narrowing the solution space.

commands.name: foreman:delegation-and-empowerment
commands.description: (foreman) Develops the daily practice of effective delegation, accountability diagnosis, and team empowerment. Covers assessing which tasks require personal attention, clarifying scope and context for delegated work, allowing productive struggle, recognising and correcting micromanagement, and leading through influence rather than control. Use when feeling overwhelmed by operational tasks, noticing accountability gaps on a team, receiving feedback about micromanagement, transitioning from individual contributor to manager, or leading a team with more expertise than oneself.

commands.name: foreman:delivering-the-deal
commands.description: (foreman) Provides the complete execution toolkit for closing negotiations: a 21-point preparation checklist, a framework for overcoming obstacles and disarming tactics, and the three-part satisfaction model for durable agreements. Includes a self-assessment instrument for measuring negotiation competence. Use when preparing for a high-stakes negotiation, when a deal has stalled or hit tactical obstacles, when managing post-deal satisfaction and buyer's remorse, or when conducting a negotiation capability audit.

commands.name: foreman:disruptive-innovation
commands.description: (foreman) Analyzes market opportunities and threats using Christensen's Disruptive Innovation theory, distinguishing between sustaining and disruptive innovation, low-end and new-market disruption. Evaluates incumbent vulnerability, asymmetric advantages, and technology improvement trajectories. Use when assessing whether a startup has a genuinely disruptive position, mapping incumbent blind spots, designing market entry strategies that avoid direct competition, defending against disruption from below, or evaluating whether to pursue low-end or new-market footholds.

commands.name: foreman:doblin-ten-types
commands.description: (foreman) Maps and designs innovation strategy using Doblin's Ten Types of Innovation across Configuration (Profit Model, Network, Structure, Process), Offering (Product Performance, Product System), and Experience (Service, Channel, Brand, Customer Engagement). Use when auditing current innovation profile, identifying competitive white space, building multi-layered defensible advantages, breaking through competitive ceilings caused by product-only innovation, or designing a new business with structural moats from inception.

commands.name: foreman:eisenhower-matrix
commands.description: (foreman) Prioritizes tasks and time allocation using the Eisenhower Matrix, classifying activities into four quadrants by urgency and importance: Do (urgent and important), Schedule (important but not urgent), Delegate (urgent but not important), and Eliminate (neither). Use when overwhelmed by competing demands, auditing how a founder spends their time, designing delegation frameworks, building QII-first weekly calendars, or shifting organizational time allocation from reactive firefighting to strategic work.

commands.name: foreman:emotional-courage
commands.description: (foreman) Builds the capacity for daily acts of leadership courage, from raising difficult issues and sharing vulnerability appropriately to channelling anxiety productively and taking principled stands. Provides incremental practices for developing courage as a skill rather than treating it as an innate trait. Use when avoiding a difficult conversation, feeling paralysed by anxiety before a high-stakes situation, sensing that you are holding back from necessary confrontation, wanting to build vulnerability into your leadership style without oversharing, or preparing to advocate for an unpopular position.

commands.name: foreman:emotional-impact-in-stories
commands.description: (foreman) Explains the singular mechanism for making audiences cry (surprise, not sadness) and two named techniques for making them laugh (Milk Cans and Baseballs, Babies and Blenders). Applies when a founder is crafting a keynote, investor narrative, brand story, or any communication designed to move an audience emotionally. Use when a story feels informative but flat, when humour falls short, or when a narrative needs to land in the heart rather than the head.

commands.name: foreman:emotional-intelligence
commands.description: (foreman) Assesses and develops leadership emotional intelligence using Goleman's five-domain EQ framework: Self-Awareness, Self-Regulation, Motivation, Empathy, and Social Skill. Diagnoses interpersonal conflicts, evaluates team EQ profiles, and builds development plans for emotional competencies.
