No photography | ~7 sections: nav > hero > logo bar (6 fake wordmarks) > 3-icon feature-card grid > 4-stat metric grid > centred CTA > one-line footer | Plain centred CTA (heading/subhead/single pill button) trailing into a generic one-line copyright footer — trails off, no address or distinct voice | none — no bespoke interaction at all, not even a scroll reveal; static Tailwind hover states only | none of the six — generic gradient-on-white SaaS look, the anti-register the others are defined against | Inter; bg #FBFAF7, text #1F2937, gradient #6366F1→#8B5CF6→#EC4899, slate grays | `anti-slop-design/sites/before-ai-slop.html` |

## Reading this table before a new build

Three grammar collisions already exist among these seven rows: Calyx,
Hyperborea and Vintergatan all read as chaptered editorial, and Vinterspelen
leans the same way with a gallery inflection. A new chaptered-editorial build
has to clear 3 more dimensions against **each** of those four rows
individually — nav treatment and hero device are the two that repeat across
them most (folio/edition-strip nav, type-in-photo or split-poster heroes), so
those are the columns most likely to collide again. Hōrai and Tidvatten share
grammar (filmic one-shot), a fixed minimal bar, a JS-parallax full-bleed
hero, and a bell-curve-scrub pinned set-piece as their signature move's
underlying mechanism — a third filmic one-shot build with a scrub-driven
pinned set-piece would need a genuinely different mechanism for the move, not
just different numbers on screen, to clear dimension 6 meaningfully even
though the gate counts it as free.

`before-ai-slop.html` is not a build to avoid colliding with — it is the
negative reference. Any real build should differ from it on every dimension
by construction.

## Alunix concept builds, rounds 1–7 (appended 2026-09-09)

Twenty-nine rows, one per built `index.html` under `anti-slop-design/tests/alunix-*`.
Every column is derived from the cell's own files: the built HTML (nav markup, section
list, `data-sc-act` attributes, `:root` custom properties, font links), its `NOTES.md`
or `BRIEF.md`, and its desktop fold screenshot read as an image. Where a cell's own
files carry no evidence for a column, the cell says `?` rather than a guess — that is a
finding about the cell's documentation, not a licence to treat the dimension as free.

Duplicates were excluded, not counted twice: `alunix-ab-r6/board/cells/*` are byte-identical
copies of the seven r6 runs, `alunix-ab-r7/board/cells/K1-1` and `K2-1` are byte-identical
copies of r6 B-K1 and B-K2 placed on r7's comparison board, and
`alunix-concepts-r5/reference/V3-baseline` is a byte-identical copy of `V3-chain`.

Rounds 1–2 and 6 predate scroll-craft integration in those cells (no `data-sc-*` in the
markup); their act shapes are hand-rolled. Rounds 3–5 and 7 run the engine. In r6 and r7,
arm A is the Claude-native control (Anthropic's `frontend-design` system prompt, no skills,

| r7 B-K1 Skymning v2 | Filmic one-shot, deliberately shared with r6 B-K1, with the other seven grammars ruled out one by one in the brief | Fixed topbar with a white/black logo swap, a label slot naming the open example page, contact right: the same pattern as r6 B-K1 and explicitly not a degree of freedom this round | A real pre-rendered 100-frame dolly push-in scrubbed frame by frame on `canvas[data-sc-sequence]`, with 104 files vendored under `assets/push/`; the window is dark at rest, showing no thumbnail of the destination | 4 engine acts plus 6 reduced-motion sections: `pin` signature act of span 5.0 > `reveal` proof > `flow` ledger > `drift` landing, using kit devices with an explicit `pin` for the reveal | The night photo opens as a `reveal` plus a `data-sc-drift` colour transition to #0b1424 under a binding hold cue; contact, address line and the generated-motion credit; nothing fades | A pre-rendered camera move that becomes a live page: the client site is masked into the window's traced opening frame by frame from `window-track.json` behind a glass layer, then swapped for the real iframe with no visible seam, and the exit shrinks a screenshot of the frame into the proof row's plate | Cinematic dark | Newsreader + Schibsted Grotesk; the same blue-hour and night photography with #0b1424 as the drift target | `anti-slop-design/tests/alunix-ab-r7/runs/B/K1/index.html` |
| r7 B-K2 Affischen v2 | Typographic poster, with the other seven grammars ruled out one by one in the brief | Thin top row: mark and wordmark, live clock and city, contact right: the same pattern as r6 B-K2 and deliberately shared | The image masked through the letters' actual measured openings using the ink-scan technique, plus one muted black-and-white documentary plate beside the wordmark, never under it and never full-bleed | 5 engine acts over 6 sections: `pin` hero of span 3 with a kinetic discrete line-height opening > reveal as wipe and grayscale > flow with stagger > reveal as hairline and glide > flow plus drift | The ground itself drifts from paper to ink, `--sc-canvas` written as `color-mix(in oklch, #1b1f1c …%, var(--paper))` with no curtain, and the page ends on its smallest type, the colophon, not on a display line | Paper behind the mask plus the breathing block: the image slides through the letters' ink form while the wordmark stands still, then the crushed block opens in one discrete step into the next headline | Editorial print | Archivo as display and Familjen Grotesk as register, roles never crossing; five colours and no chromatic accent, paper oklch(85% 0.028 135), ink oklch(22% 0.012 150) | `anti-slop-design/tests/alunix-ab-r7/runs/B/K2/index.html` |

### What these rows share, and what the next Alunix build has to avoid

Grammar has been spent hard. Chaptered editorial now has five rows here (r1 K4, r2 R2, R3,
R4, r4 M2) on top of the four seed rows, filmic one-shot has four (r6 A-K1, B-K1,
B-K1-nogate, r7 B-K1) on top of two seed rows, and typographic poster has five (r1 K3, r2
R6, r6 A-K2 and B-K2, r7 B-K2). Continuous world is a five-row family (M1, V1, V2, V3,
V3b) that also shares nav treatment and close pattern by construction, because every r5
variant inherited M1's chrome and its two closing objects; those five rows clear the gate
against each other only on hero device, act shape and signature move, which is exactly 3
of the 5 non-free dimensions, the bare minimum. A sixth build in that family would have
nowhere left to differ.

Two nav patterns repeat across rounds and should be treated as used up: the thin
scrolling top row with wordmark and contact (M1, V1, V2, V3, V3b) and the fixed minimal
bar with logo left and contact right that darkens or lightens per ground (r6 A-K1, B-K1,
B-K1-nogate, r7 B-K1). Two hero devices likewise: the full-bleed blue-hour photograph
with a light-serif headline in the water (four rows) and the crushed poster wordmark with
the example screenshots showing through or beside the letters (four rows). The r7 rows
record their own shared dimensions honestly — each clears the gate at exactly 4 of 6
against its r6 predecessor, with grammar and nav knowingly shared — so a v3 of either
concept cannot reuse the hero device, the act shape or the close as well.

Ten rows carried `?` in Register when the r1–r7 block was first appended: r2 R3, R4 and
R5, the r3 build, r4 M1 and M2, and r5 V1, V2, V3 and V3b. Those cells' own files name
grammar, world and palette but never a register from the six-name vocabulary, and no
sibling file names it for them either. On 2026-09-09 the column was filled for all ten by
reading each cell's `index.html` directly (and, for the r3 build and r4 M2, its 1440 fold
as pixels) against `design/SKILL.md`'s register table and its "what varies with register"
markers: face, grain, buttons versus typeset links, ground and subject. Every one of the
ten reads as **modern clean** — one lineage, sans display with mono as register only, no
serif and no grain anywhere, one blue accent, ledgers over cards, and a precision subject
— which is the same read the registry already recorded for r1 K1, K2, K5, K6 and r2 R1
and R2. Each cell states the file it was derived from, so the derivation is auditable and
declared as post-hoc, exactly like the seven seed rows above.

12	register: editorial print
13	grammar: gallery/catalog
14	lane: "A cream-and-ink portfolio that opens on a huge whisper-thin didone headline over capsule-shaped project tiles in full client colour, then closes on one dramatic ink-black panel where the yellow accent finally appears"
15	mode: persuade
16	traits: ["160px whisper-thin didone display", "97% achromatic UI, client colour in work only", "800px capsule image radius", "tracked-out 0.107em small type", "single dark footer inversion", "circular rotating text badge"]
17	palette: ["#111118", "#ffffff", "#dddddd", "#bdbdbd", "#7c7c7c", "#fef199"]
18	type: ["Editorial New", "PP Mori"]
19	measured: designlang (confirmed)
20	kind: reference-style
21	source: anton

24	---
25	
26	## Why it works
27	
28	Palette and type are read from Refero's extracted tokens. The studio's own UI stays
29	97% achromatic — ink black `#111118` and paper white carry almost everything — which
30	means the one place colour is allowed to exist, the work itself, reads as maximally
31	vivid by contrast. Capsule-shaped project tiles (800px radius, practically a
32	lozenge) bleed whatever client palette they carry straight onto the cream page, so
33	the portfolio grid becomes a controlled burst of colour inside an otherwise
34	disciplined frame.
35	
36	Type does the same restraint-then-release move as the page's colour: PP Mori
37	carries every functional voice (nav, labels, body) at weights 200-600 with an
38	unusually wide 0.107em tracking on small sizes, while Editorial New — a didone
39	serif at weight 200 only — is reserved exclusively for display headlines from 48px
40	up to 160px. Because the thin serif never appears below 48px and the sans never
41	carries a display headline, the pairing reads as two distinct instruments rather
42	than a font stack.
43	
44	The single dramatic gesture is saved for the end: the entire page is light until
45	the footer, which inverts to `#111118` and is the only place the highlighter-yellow
46	`#fef199` accent appears — outlining a massive pill CTA. Holding one colour and one
47	inversion in reserve for the close makes the last screen feel like a different room,
48	not a louder button.
49	
50	## What to borrow (principle)
51	
52	- **Let client/project colour be the only colour.** A near-achromatic studio UI
53	  makes a portfolio grid read as more vivid, not less, because nothing competes
54	  with it.
55	- **Reserve an accent for exactly one section.** Saving a colour for the footer
56	  alone turns the close into an event instead of diluting the accent everywhere.
57	- **Pair one ultra-thin display face with one workhorse sans, never at the same
58	  size.** A 200-weight serif above 48px against a 200-600 weight sans below it
59	  keeps the tension legible instead of muddy.
60	- **Use one dramatic shape as a signature, sparingly.** An 800px "capsule" image
61	  radius reads as a device precisely because nothing else on the page shares it.
62	- **Track out small type generously.** 0.107em letter-spacing at 12-15px is what
63	  makes nav and labels read as fashion-editorial rather than default UI.
64	
65	## What to leave
66	
67	- The "Don't" list is empty in the source export — the system's constraints are
68	  implicit in its Do's, which makes fidelity harder to check without the live site.
69	- An 800px capsule radius depends on generous card width; at narrow/mobile
70	  breakpoints it will collapse toward a pill or a circle, losing the lozenge shape.
71	- A single reserved accent colour for one section only works if that section is
72	  genuinely the page's close — used mid-page it would read as an unexplained
73	  one-off.
74	
75	## Signature move
76	
77	The circular rotating text badge — "AVAILABLE NOW" set on an invisible circle,
78	used once as a floating decorative element beside the hero headline rather than as
79	a repeatable component. It is deliberately not part of the design system; it is a
80	single ornament.
81	
82	## Motion
83	
84	(from designlang extract) Feel reads as smooth, and the page is scroll-linked.
85	Interactive transitions run on a plain `ease` curve at three short durations —
86	100ms, 200ms and 300ms — the fastest tier for hover/colour changes, the slowest for
87	larger reveals; the broader transition log adds a 400ms opacity fade for section
88	entrances. The one keyframe confirmed in use is `slide`, a slide-x transform (3
89	uses) driving translateX motion — most likely the capsule-tile image slider/marquee
90	behaviour rather than the rotating text badge, since no rotate keyframe registers
91	as in-use (a `spin` keyframe exists in the stylesheet but isn't confirmed firing).
92	(observed in capture) the capsule-shaped image containers and the circular rotating
93	badge suggest the badge text itself may continuously rotate, and hover states on
94	ghost/filled pill buttons likely invert fill and text colour rather than adding
95	movement — consistent with the flat, shadow-free, editorial register of the rest of
96	the system.
97	
98	| Token | Value | Easing |
99	|---|---|---|
100	| xs | 100ms | `ease` |
101	| sm | 200ms | `ease` |
102	| md | 300ms | `ease` |
103	| slide keyframe | — | translateX, 3 uses |
104	
105	## Brief
106	
107	Build a visual-design-studio portfolio. Canvas is paper white, ink is near-black
108	`#111118`, with soft-ash and stone-gray for muted borders and dividers — the whole
109	UI stays achromatic except for the highlighter-yellow `#fef199` reserved for the
110	footer only. Open on a full-width Editorial New weight-200 headline (48-160px,
111	line-height 1.0, no uppercase) stating the studio's promise in one or two lines.
112	Below, lay out a portfolio grid of capsule-shaped project tiles (800px radius,
113	8px on the outer card) bleeding full client-project colour and imagery. Use PP Mori
114	at 0.107em tracking for all nav, labels and body copy; reserve 24px pill radius for
115	buttons and 8px for cards and links. Add one floating circular rotating text badge
116	near the hero as a one-off ornament. Close on a full-width `#111118` inverted
117	footer panel with a giant 150px-radius CTA pill outlined in highlighter yellow.
118	
119	## Image recipe
120	
121	Not applicable as a primary photographic recipe — the site's imagery is client
122	project work (screenshots, illustration, branded colour blocks) rather than
123	photography. Where a portrait or process shot is needed: a plain, evenly lit studio
124	headshot or workspace detail of [SUBJECT], neutral background, no heavy retouching,
125	consistent with an achromatic UI that lets the subject's own colour read clean.
126	
127	## Photo search
128	
129	Unsplash first, Pexels second.
130	- "designer workspace desk minimal flat lay"
131	- "portrait studio lighting neutral background"
132	- "laptop screen mockup UI design work"
133	- "colour palette swatches paper minimal"
134	
135	## Reference lock
136	
137	Primary reference/direction: André Cândido — near-monochrome editorial portfolio,
138	whisper-thin didone display, colour reserved for client work and one footer accent.
139	Preserve (3-5 traits): 97% achromatic UI (`#111118` ink on white); Editorial New
140	weight 200 exclusively for display headlines 48px and above, never smaller, never
141	heavier; PP Mori at 0.107em tracking for all functional text; 800px capsule radius
142	on portfolio images vs. 8px on cards and 24px on buttons; a single dark `#111118`
143	footer inversion where highlighter yellow `#fef199` appears for the first and only
144	time.
145	Borrow only (1-2): the circular rotating "AVAILABLE NOW" text badge; the 150px-
146	radius oversized footer CTA pill.
147	Role rules: yellow never appears outside the footer panel; serif never carries body
148	copy or UI labels; sans never sets a display headline; client-project colour is the
149	only large colour field permitted pre-footer.
150	Media strategy: none (no external photography) — client-work screenshots and
151	colour blocks carry all chromatic content; any supplementary photography stays
152	neutral and desaturated to match the UI.
153	Reject: a second accent colour anywhere outside the footer; rounded corners below
154	8px or above 24px except the 800px image capsule; shadows or elevation; a bolded
155	Editorial New headline.
156	Token commitments: bg `#ffffff`, ink `#111118`, border `#dddddd`/`#bdbdbd`, muted
157	text `#7c7c7c`, footer accent `#fef199`; display weight 200 at 48-160px/leading 1.0;
158	body PP Mori 200-600 at 12-24px, 0.107em tracking on 12-15px sizes; radius 8px
159	cards, 24px buttons, 800px images, 150px footer CTA; base spacing unit 8px, section
160	gap 80-120px.

## Reference lock

Primary reference/direction: André Cândido — near-monochrome editorial portfolio,
whisper-thin didone display, colour reserved for client work and one footer accent.
Preserve (3-5 traits): 97% achromatic UI (`#111118` ink on white); Editorial New
weight 200 exclusively for display headlines 48px and above, never smaller, never
heavier; PP Mori at 0.107em tracking for all functional text; 800px capsule radius
on portfolio images vs. 8px on cards and 24px on buttons; a single dark `#111118`
footer inversion where highlighter yellow `#fef199` appears for the first and only
time.
Borrow only (1-2): the circular rotating "AVAILABLE NOW" text badge; the 150px-
radius oversized footer CTA pill.
Role rules: yellow never appears outside the footer panel; serif never carries body
copy or UI labels; sans never sets a display headline; client-project colour is the
only large colour field permitted pre-footer.
Media strategy: none (no external photography) — client-work screenshots and
colour blocks carry all chromatic content; any supplementary photography stays
neutral and desaturated to match the UI.
Reject: a second accent colour anywhere outside the footer; rounded corners below
8px or above 24px except the 800px image capsule; shadows or elevation; a bolded
Editorial New headline.
Token commitments: bg `#ffffff`, ink `#111118`, border `#dddddd`/`#bdbdbd`, muted
text `#7c7c7c`, footer accent `#fef199`; display weight 200 at 48-160px/leading 1.0;
body PP Mori 200-600 at 12-24px, 0.107em tracking on 12-15px sizes; radius 8px
cards, 24px buttons, 800px images, 150px footer CTA; base spacing unit 8px, section
gap 80-120px.

26	## Why it works
27	
28	The page opens between two moving marquee tickers — a thin cream strip above
29	the nav ("THE SCENT OF EXPENSIVE HOBBIES IS HERE") and a bold red strip below
30	the hero ("THIS IS NOT A BEAUTY BRAND") — so the brand's attitude is stated in
31	motion before any product is shown. The hero photograph itself (a clay tennis
32	court, balls mid-bounce) has nothing to do with the product literally; it's
33	establishing a lifestyle register — leisure, expense, ritual — that the
34	condensed all-caps headline ("WELLNESS ROOTED IN RITUAL, ART, AND DROP
35	CULTURE") then names directly.
36	
37	One display face, Anton — extremely condensed, extremely bold — carries every
38	headline, ticker and section statement at consistent weight, so scale is the
39	only variable used for emphasis; nothing shifts in style, only in size. Body
40	copy and product data drop to a plain Inter, keeping the loud parts loud and
41	the informational parts quiet. Product cards run on a black ground with cream
42	frames, a red "on sale" flag, and product photography with visible packaging
43	copy (the products themselves are typeset like the site, condensed bold
44	labels) — so the packaging and the page share one visual system rather than
45	photography being the only brand touchpoint.
46	
47	The "Our Why" section breaks from product entirely into a dark maroon panel
48	with archival-style photography and a direct, culturally specific statement
49	("EVEN WHILE SLEEPING, BLACK PEOPLE CANNOT REST") — copy doing real narrative
50	work rather than generic brand-voice copy, which is unusual enough in this
51	genre to be the site's strongest asset.
52	
53	## What to borrow (principle)
54	
55	- **Use scrolling marquee tickers as attitude statements**, not just
56	  promotional banners — putting the brand's point of view in constant motion
57	  makes it unmissable without a large static block.
58	- **Choose hero photography for register, not for product literalism** — a
59	  tennis court says "expensive leisure" faster than a product shot would.
60	- **Run one extremely condensed, extremely bold display face at every scale**
61	  so hierarchy comes entirely from size, keeping the whole page visually
62	  coherent even across very different section types.
63	- **Let real, specific, culturally-grounded copy carry a "why" section** —
64	  it reads as conviction, not as brand-voice filler.
65	- **Match product packaging typography to the site's own type system** so
66	  photography and page feel like one continuous brand object.
67	
68	## What to leave
69	
70	- The email-signup modal fires early and covers most of the hero on load —
71	  worth testing timing/frequency against how much of the marquee/hero attitude
72	  gets seen before it's obscured.
73	- Two marquee tickers running simultaneously (top and bottom of hero) plus a
74	  third mid-page risks becoming visual noise rather than emphasis if overused
75	  further down the page.
76	- Extremely condensed display type at small sizes (as seen in some award/press
77	  captions) pushes legibility — fine at headline scale, marginal at caption
78	  scale.

82	Twin scrolling marquee tickers bracketing the hero — one understated
83	(top nav strip), one loud and red ("THIS IS NOT A BEAUTY BRAND") — stating the
84	brand's point of view in constant motion before any product appears.

mode: persuade
traits: ["scrolling marquee ticker text (top and bottom)", "condensed bold display sans (Anton)", "black ground with red accent", "cream product-card panels", "press-logo wall", "archival family photography", "email signup modal", "accessibility widget button"]
palette: ["#000000", "#FFF8E7", "#C00121", "#887871", "#212018", "#E2DACC", "#703D2E", "#A99E93"]

measured: designlang (confirmed)

## Why it works

The page opens between two moving marquee tickers — a thin cream strip above
the nav ("THE SCENT OF EXPENSIVE HOBBIES IS HERE") and a bold red strip below
the hero ("THIS IS NOT A BEAUTY BRAND") — so the brand's attitude is stated in
motion before any product is shown. The hero photograph itself (a clay tennis
court, balls mid-bounce) has nothing to do with the product literally; it's
establishing a lifestyle register — leisure, expense, ritual — that the
condensed all-caps headline ("WELLNESS ROOTED IN RITUAL, ART, AND DROP
CULTURE") then names directly.

One display face, Anton — extremely condensed, extremely bold — carries every
headline, ticker and section statement at consistent weight, so scale is the
only variable used for emphasis; nothing shifts in style, only in size. Body
copy and product data drop to a plain Inter, keeping the loud parts loud and
the informational parts quiet. Product cards run on a black ground with cream
frames, a red "on sale" flag, and product photography with visible packaging
copy (the products themselves are typeset like the site, condensed bold
labels) — so the packaging and the page share one visual system rather than
photography being the only brand touchpoint.

The "Our Why" section breaks from product entirely into a dark maroon panel
with archival-style photography and a direct, culturally specific statement
("EVEN WHILE SLEEPING, BLACK PEOPLE CANNOT REST") — copy doing real narrative
work rather than generic brand-voice copy, which is unusual enough in this
genre to be the site's strongest asset.

## What to borrow (principle)

- **Use scrolling marquee tickers as attitude statements**, not just
  promotional banners — putting the brand's point of view in constant motion
  makes it unmissable without a large static block.
- **Choose hero photography for register, not for product literalism** — a
  tennis court says "expensive leisure" faster than a product shot would.
- **Run one extremely condensed, extremely bold display face at every scale**
  so hierarchy comes entirely from size, keeping the whole page visually
  coherent even across very different section types.
- **Let real, specific, culturally-grounded copy carry a "why" section** —
  it reads as conviction, not as brand-voice filler.
- **Match product packaging typography to the site's own type system** so
  photography and page feel like one continuous brand object.

## What to leave

- The email-signup modal fires early and covers most of the hero on load —
  worth testing timing/frequency against how much of the marquee/hero attitude
  gets seen before it's obscured.
- Two marquee tickers running simultaneously (top and bottom of hero) plus a
  third mid-page risks becoming visual noise rather than emphasis if overused
  further down the page.
- Extremely condensed display type at small sizes (as seen in some award/press
  captions) pushes legibility — fine at headline scale, marginal at caption
  scale.

## Signature move

Twin scrolling marquee tickers bracketing the hero — one understated
(top nav strip), one loud and red ("THIS IS NOT A BEAUTY BRAND") — stating the
brand's point of view in constant motion before any product appears.

## Motion

(from designlang extract) The extract rates overall feel "responsive" with
confirmed scroll-linked behaviour. Five duration steps span 100ms to 800ms,
mostly on a snappy custom ease-out (`cubic-bezier(0.3, 1, 0.3, 1)`, 107
uses — the dominant curve on the page) with three more measured custom curves
(30 uses combined) for slower transitions. Four keyframes are confirmed
in use: `scrolling-left` (transform + visibility, 22 uses) is the mechanism
behind the marquee tickers; `rotator` and `dash` (7 uses each) drive a
rotating/SVG-progress element; `junipNodeInserted` (1 use) is a third-party
review-widget (Junip) insertion animation, not brand motion. Additional
keyframes — `text-underlined` (a link-hover underline wipe), `zoom-fade` /
`zoom-fade-short` (scale 1.1-1.2→1 with fade), and `spin` — are defined in the
stylesheet but not registered as in-use at scan time. (observed in capture)
The marquee ticker text is a continuous horizontal scroll/loop, confirmed by
the raw and fresh captures showing different text scroll positions on the
same strip. An email-signup modal appears over the hero within the first few
seconds of load (observed — present in the fresh capture, absent in the raw
one), suggesting a timed rather than scroll-triggered trigger.

## Brief

Build a DTC lifestyle/wellness brand around one moving marquee ticker stating
the brand's attitude in a short, quotable line, bracketing a hero photograph
chosen for lifestyle register rather than literal product content. Run one
extremely condensed, extremely bold display face at every heading scale, with

entirely — a dark accent panel with archival-style photography and specific,
first-person copy stating why the brand exists, not generic mission language.

photography reads as part of the same system.

colour grading evoking film stock, candid or environmental framing rather than
studio product staging, chosen to establish a lifestyle or cultural register
connected to the brand rather than to depict the product literally.

26	## Why it works
27	
28	The page is a white sheet and it never pretends otherwise. Everything that is not the
29	sheet is a rounded object placed on it: the hero photograph with a flat green block
30	offset behind it, three case cards in their own grounds, five customer logos in bordered
31	cards, a support card, and finally a footer that slides in as a second sheet with a
32	rounded top edge. Because every object shares the same 24 px corner, the page reads as
33	one material system even though its sections carry very different content. The grotesk
34	does the rest: one weight (600) for every heading from the 84 px H1 down to the 34 px
35	card title, so hierarchy is size alone, and a plain 20 px body in a second sans.
36	
37	The process is the page's one structural device. "Så arbetar vi" is a vertical timeline,
38	a pink hairline with plum dots, one dot per phase (four phases on /tjanster/hemsida:
39	Uppstart och strategi, Design och utveckling, Innehåll, Lansering), each phase paired
40	with a 3D blob render on the right. In the capture the phase text had not revealed
41	(the reveal is scroll-triggered and the capture ran under a reduced-motion setting), so
42	the slices show the skeleton of the device rather than its words: the line, the dots and
43	the blobs carry the section even without copy, which is the skeleton test passed.
44	
45	Colour is rationed by role. The plum (`#624058`) is the only filled button and the
46	timeline dot; the pink (`#EC8AA3`) is the wordmark, the breadcrumb's current page, the
47	timeline line and the case-card title; the green block behind the hero photo appears
48	once. Nothing else on the sheet is chromatic, so the three colours are legible as three
49	jobs. The read is offset by two persistent widgets, a chat bubble and a cookie card, that
50	sit in every viewport and compete with the hero for the lower-left corner.
51

53	
54	- **Name the phases of the work and give each one a fixed place on a line.** The
55	  timeline says "this is a sequence with a beginning and an end" before a word is read.
56	- **One corner radius for every object on the sheet**, so cards, photos and the footer
57	  read as one material.
58	- **One heading weight; hierarchy by size only.**
59	- **A named person as the contact**, not a form: the reader knows who answers.
60	- **A flat colour block offset behind the hero photograph** as the only depth device.
61	
62	## What to leave

64	- Three equal case cards and five equal logo cards: the template rhythm TASTE § 5 counts
65	  at zero in Anton's own sources.
66	- The persistent chat widget and the cookie card that sit in the fold on every screen.
67	- Reveal-on-scroll that leaves the timeline empty when motion is gated by the OS

70	- Customer logos, a Google Partner badge and a named team member: PRODUCT.md § absences
71	  forbids all three for Alunix.

73	## Signature move
74	
75	The process as a vertical timeline: a pink hairline runs down the left margin, a plum dot
76	marks each phase, and each phase owns one 3D render on the right, so the work reads as a
77	line the reader travels rather than four cards.

82	`ease-out` and one custom `cubic-bezier(0.445, 0.05, 0.55, 0.95)`. One keyframe in use,

kind: reference-style
source: claude

## Why it works

The page is a white sheet and it never pretends otherwise. Everything that is not the
sheet is a rounded object placed on it: the hero photograph with a flat green block
offset behind it, three case cards in their own grounds, five customer logos in bordered
cards, a support card, and finally a footer that slides in as a second sheet with a
rounded top edge. Because every object shares the same 24 px corner, the page reads as
one material system even though its sections carry very different content. The grotesk
does the rest: one weight (600) for every heading from the 84 px H1 down to the 34 px
card title, so hierarchy is size alone, and a plain 20 px body in a second sans.

The process is the page's one structural device. "Så arbetar vi" is a vertical timeline,
a pink hairline with plum dots, one dot per phase (four phases on /tjanster/hemsida:
Uppstart och strategi, Design och utveckling, Innehåll, Lansering), each phase paired
with a 3D blob render on the right. In the capture the phase text had not revealed
(the reveal is scroll-triggered and the capture ran under a reduced-motion setting), so
the slices show the skeleton of the device rather than its words: the line, the dots and
the blobs carry the section even without copy, which is the skeleton test passed.

Colour is rationed by role. The plum (`#624058`) is the only filled button and the
timeline dot; the pink (`#EC8AA3`) is the wordmark, the breadcrumb's current page, the
timeline line and the case-card title; the green block behind the hero photo appears
once. Nothing else on the sheet is chromatic, so the three colours are legible as three
jobs. The read is offset by two persistent widgets, a chat bubble and a cookie card, that
sit in every viewport and compete with the hero for the lower-left corner.

## What to borrow (principle)

- **Name the phases of the work and give each one a fixed place on a line.** The
  timeline says "this is a sequence with a beginning and an end" before a word is read.
- **One corner radius for every object on the sheet**, so cards, photos and the footer
  read as one material.
- **One heading weight; hierarchy by size only.**
- **A named person as the contact**, not a form: the reader knows who answers.
- **A flat colour block offset behind the hero photograph** as the only depth device.

## What to leave

- Three equal case cards and five equal logo cards: the template rhythm TASTE § 5 counts
  at zero in Anton's own sources.
- The persistent chat widget and the cookie card that sit in the fold on every screen.
- Reveal-on-scroll that leaves the timeline empty when motion is gated by the OS
  setting: F-011 forbids the gate outright.
- The `→` suffix on `Se alla case` (gate 97) and the breadcrumb.
- Customer logos, a Google Partner badge and a named team member: PRODUCT.md § absences
  forbids all three for Alunix.

## Signature move

The process as a vertical timeline: a pink hairline runs down the left margin, a plum dot
marks each phase, and each phase owns one 3D render on the right, so the work reads as a
line the reader travels rather than four cards.

## Motion

Feel "smooth", scroll-linked. Durations 100 to 800 ms, `ease` on 34 of 36 transitions, one
`ease-out` and one custom `cubic-bezier(0.445, 0.05, 0.55, 0.95)`. One keyframe in use,
`infiniteScroll` (a `transform` marquee, used twice, the logo carousel on mobile). The
timeline phases are revealed on scroll; under a reduced-motion setting the reveal never
fired and the phase copy stayed hidden in the capture, which is the one thing this page
does with motion and the one thing it gets wrong for this design system. No parallax, no
pin, no scrub. (from designlang extract, plus the captured slices)

## Brief

Build a service page for a web agency on a plain white sheet: pink wordmark top left, a
pill CTA row top right, a breadcrumb, then a two-line black grotesk H1 with an H2 and a
short paragraph on the left and one photograph on the right with a flat colour block

<!doctype html>
<html lang="sv">
<head>
<meta charset="utf-8">
<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width,initial-scale=1">
<title>ALUNIX</title>
<link rel="stylesheet" href="assets/vendor/lenis.css">

<style>
@font-face{
  font-family:"Geist";
  src:url("assets/fonts/geist-500-latin.woff2") format("woff2");
  font-weight:500; font-style:normal; font-display:swap;
}
@font-face{
  font-family:"Geist Mono";
  src:url("assets/fonts/geist-mono-400-latin.woff2") format("woff2");
  font-weight:400; font-style:normal; font-display:swap;
}

:root{
  --paper:#ffffff;
  --ink:#232323;
  --black:#000000;
  --grey:#d9d9d9;
  --mint:#0af474;
  --mint-soft:#a3fbcb;
  --rust:#9c5a3a;
  --lacquer:#b23524;
  --seam:1px solid #000;

  --headline-50:clamp(3.25rem, 0.418rem + 12.082vw, 12.5rem);
  --headline-40:clamp(2.5rem, 1.352rem + 4.9vw, 6.25rem);
  --headline-20:clamp(2rem, 1.694rem + 1.306vw, 3rem);
  --h3:38px;
  --body:16px;
  --body-30:clamp(1.5rem, 1.347rem + 0.653vw, 2rem);
  --caption:13px;
  --cellpad:20px;
}

*{box-sizing:border-box;}
html{color-scheme:light;}
body{
  margin:0;
  background:#000;
  color:var(--ink);
  font-family:"Geist","Arial",system-ui,sans-serif;
  font-weight:500;
  line-height:1.3;
  -webkit-font-smoothing:antialiased;
  overflow-x:hidden;
}
img{display:block;max-width:100%;}
.mono{font-family:"Geist Mono","Consolas",monospace;font-weight:400;}
h1,h2,h3,p,ol,ul,figure{margin:0;padding:0;}
a{color:inherit;}
.sr-only{position:absolute;width:1px;height:1px;padding:0;margin:-1px;overflow:hidden;clip:rect(0,0,0,0);white-space:nowrap;border:0;}

/* ---------------------------------------------------------- rutverket shell */
.rutverk{max-width:1440px;margin:0 auto;background:#000;}
.rutverk > section{scroll-margin-top:48px;}

.g{display:grid;gap:1px;background:#000;}
.cell{background:var(--paper);padding:var(--cellpad);position:relative;overflow:hidden;}
.cell--pad0{padding:0;}
.cell--ink{background:var(--ink);color:var(--paper);}
.cell--black{background:var(--black);color:var(--paper);}
.cell--grey{background:var(--grey);color:var(--ink);}
.cell--mint{background:var(--mint);color:var(--black);}
.cell--rust{background:var(--rust);color:var(--paper);}
.cell--lacquer{background:var(--lacquer);color:var(--paper);}

.g12{grid-template-columns:repeat(12,1fr);}
@media (max-width:1199px){
  .g12{grid-template-columns:repeat(6,1fr);}
}
@media (max-width:767px){
  .g12{grid-template-columns:1fr;}
  .g12 > *{grid-column:1 / -1 !important;}
}

.c-2{grid-column:span 2;}
.c-3{grid-column:span 3;}
.c-4{grid-column:span 4;}
.c-5{grid-column:span 5;}
.c-6{grid-column:span 6;}
.c-7{grid-column:span 7;}
.c-8{grid-column:span 8;}
.c-12{grid-column:span 12;}
@media (max-width:1199px){
  .c-7,.c-5,.c-8,.c-4{grid-column:span 6;}
}

.headline-50{font-size:var(--headline-50);line-height:.8;letter-spacing:-.04em;font-weight:500;}
.headline-40{font-size:var(--headline-40);line-height:1;letter-spacing:-.04em;font-weight:500;}
.headline-20{font-size:var(--headline-20);line-height:1;letter-spacing:-.04em;font-weight:500;}
.h3{font-size:var(--h3);line-height:1.1;letter-spacing:-.02em;font-weight:500;}
.body{font-size:var(--body);line-height:1.3;letter-spacing:-.02em;}
.body-30{font-size:var(--body-30);line-height:1.1;letter-spacing:-.02em;}
.caption{font-size:var(--caption);letter-spacing:0;}
.tnum{font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums;}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------- topline */
.topline{
  position:sticky;top:0;z-index:40;height:48px;max-width:1440px;margin:0 auto;
  display:grid;grid-template-columns:auto 1fr auto;gap:1px;background:#000;
}
.topline-cell{background:var(--black);color:var(--paper);display:flex;align-items:center;padding:0 20px;}
.topline-logo{width:auto;height:22px;}
.topline-mark{font-size:15px;letter-spacing:-.02em;font-weight:500;}
.topline-mid{background:var(--paper);}
.topline-contact{background:var(--black);color:var(--paper);font-size:14px;text-decoration:none;justify-content:flex-end;}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------- hero */
/* R3: the fixed 190svh CSS-sticky stage is gone. The pin distance is now
   owned by ScrollTrigger's own pinSpacing (desktop matchMedia branch,
   RORELSE-SPEC.md §2); hero-wrap just needs to size to its content so a
   no-JS/pre-JS view still shows one full stage, not a dead 90svh gap. */
.hero-wrap{position:relative;max-width:1440px;margin:0 auto;}
.hero-stage{
  position:relative;height:calc(100svh - 48px);
  display:grid;grid-template-columns:1fr 1fr;grid-template-rows:1fr 1fr;
  gap:1px;background:#000;
}
@media (max-width:767px){
  /* Mobile drops the pin: no extra scroll-span, no sticky stage. The four
     cells stack in normal flow (each already min-height:60vw, so the
     stack is naturally taller than one screen) and the card flips against
     that natural scroll distance instead of a dedicated dead-space span. */
  .hero-wrap{height:auto;}
  .hero-stage{grid-template-columns:1fr;grid-template-rows:repeat(4,minmax(60vw,auto));height:auto;position:relative;top:0;}
}
.hero-cell{position:relative;overflow:hidden;}
.hero-ov{background:var(--paper);display:flex;align-items:flex-end;padding:var(--cellpad);}
.hero-oh{background:var(--grey);}
.hero-nv{background:var(--grey);}
.hero-nh{background:var(--mint);}
.hero-h1{max-width:14ch;}

.dither-layer{position:absolute;inset:0;width:100%;height:100%;object-fit:cover;}
.color-layer{position:absolute;inset:0;width:100%;height:100%;object-fit:cover;}

/* card: a physical object (light stock, ink edge, hard offset shadow) so
   it reads against a black cell instead of disappearing into it. ~1.6x
   the R1 size at 1440 (was ~340px wide, now ~520px), 85:55 kept. */
.card-anchor{
  position:absolute;left:75%;top:50%;
  width:min(36vw,520px);
  aspect-ratio:85/55;
  transform:translate(-50%,-50%);
  perspective:1600px;
  z-index:5;
  pointer-events:none;
}
@media (max-width:767px){ .card-anchor{left:50%;top:120vw;width:min(74vw,380px);} }
.card-flip{
  width:100%;height:100%;position:relative;
  transform-style:preserve-3d;
  transform:rotateY(calc(var(--flip,0) * 180deg));
  box-shadow:10px 10px 0 0 #000;
}
.face{
  position:absolute;inset:0;
  background:#fff;
  backface-visibility:hidden;
  border:1px solid #000;
  overflow:hidden;
}
/* A visible white mat around the photo, not a full-bleed image: a card
   that is a photo edge-to-edge reads as "the photo", not as "a light
   stock object sitting on the cell" - the mat is what makes the white
   stock actually visible against a black ÖH ground. */
.face--front{background:#fff;padding:6%;}
/* R6 bugfix: kontakt's front is a <button> wrapping <span>s (spans, unlike
   hero's <div>s, default to display:inline) - an inline, merely
   position:relative .photo never gets a real box (width/height are ignored
   on non-replaced inline elements), so it collapsed to a ~2px sliver and
   the absolutely-positioned img inside inherited that zero-size containing
   block. display:block here makes both tags behave identically. */
.face--front .photo{display:block;position:relative;width:100%;height:100%;overflow:hidden;border:1px solid rgba(0,0,0,.5);}
.face--back{
  transform:rotateY(180deg);
  background:#fff;color:var(--ink);
  display:flex;flex-direction:column;justify-content:center;gap:10px;padding:6% 8%;
}
.face--front img{position:absolute;inset:0;width:100%;height:100%;object-fit:cover;}
.mark-dock{position:absolute;top:9%;left:9%;width:14%;z-index:2;}
.mark-dock svg{width:100%;height:auto;fill:#fff;filter:drop-shadow(0 0 3px rgba(0,0,0,.7));}
.card-mark{font-size:clamp(20px,2.6vw,32px);letter-spacing:-.02em;margin:0;}
.card-kicker{font-family:"Geist Mono";font-weight:400;font-size:clamp(11px,1.1vw,14px);opacity:.65;margin:2px 0 0;}
.card-rule{border:0;border-top:1px solid rgba(0,0,0,.25);margin:6px 0;width:100%;}
.card-services{display:flex;gap:10px;font-family:"Geist Mono";font-weight:400;font-size:clamp(10px,1.1vw,13px);}
.card-cta{font-size:clamp(13px,1.5vw,18px);text-decoration:underline;margin-top:4px;}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------- tes */
.tes-top{background:var(--black);color:var(--paper);padding:calc(var(--cellpad)*2) var(--cellpad);}
.tes-top .headline-50{max-width:22ch;}
.tes-lower{min-height:104svh;}
.tes-stack{display:grid;grid-template-rows:repeat(3,1fr);gap:1px;background:#000;}
.tes-line{padding:var(--cellpad);display:flex;align-items:center;}
.tes-image{padding:0;}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------- process */
.process-row{}
.process-left{background:var(--grey);}
.process-sticky{position:sticky;top:calc(48px + var(--cellpad));}
.process-kicker{margin-bottom:14px;}
.process-title{margin:0 0 18px;max-width:11ch;}
.process-lock{max-width:32ch;opacity:.8;}
.process-image{position:relative;margin-top:32px;aspect-ratio:1/1;width:100%;max-width:680px;border:1px solid #000;overflow:hidden;}
.process-right{background:var(--black);color:var(--paper);padding:0;}
.process-steps{list-style:none;}
.process-row-item{display:grid;grid-template-columns:56px 1fr;gap:14px;padding:22px var(--cellpad);border-top:1px solid #000;}
.process-row-item:first-child{border-top:none;}
.process-num{font-family:"Geist Mono";font-weight:400;font-size:13px;padding-top:4px;}
.process-step-title{margin:0 0 6px;}
.process-p{color:#bdbdbd;max-width:56ch;font-size:15px;}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------- exempelcase */
/* R5 §A bugfix: 0.6x bottom padding (12px) was less than the SplitText
   mask-breathe allowance (0.16em, ~16-20px at this clamp size) needs to
   clear the word's own descenders before the cell's overflow:hidden edge
   - verify_motion.py's legibility scan caught the word's rendered box
   (with its mask wrapper's padding-bottom) genuinely sitting a few px
   below the cell's clip boundary at every scroll position (0vh visible,
   not >=40vh). Matching the top padding removes the clip entirely. */
.case-word-cell{padding:calc(var(--cellpad)*1.4) var(--cellpad) calc(var(--cellpad)*1.4 + 4px);overflow:hidden;}
.case-word-cell .headline-50{max-width:100%;}

/* R5 §B1: väljaren - två knappar, skarpa 1440x900-vyer, ingen beskärande zoom */
.case-picker-cell{padding:0 var(--cellpad) calc(var(--cellpad)*1.2);background:#000;}
.case-picker{display:grid;gap:1px;background:#000;}
.case-choice{
  display:block;width:100%;margin:0;padding:0;border:0;background:var(--paper);color:inherit;
  font:inherit;text-align:left;cursor:pointer;-webkit-appearance:none;appearance:none;
}
.case-choice-frame{position:relative;display:block;aspect-ratio:16/10;overflow:hidden;background:var(--grey);}
.case-choice-frame img{position:absolute;inset:0;width:100%;height:100%;object-fit:cover;transform:scale(1);transition:transform .7s cubic-bezier(.23,1,.32,1);}
@media (hover:hover){
  .case-choice:hover .case-choice-frame img,
  .case-choice:focus-visible .case-choice-frame img{transform:scale(1.04);}
}
.case-choice:focus-visible{outline:3px solid var(--black);outline-offset:-3px;}
.case-choice-meta{display:block;padding:16px var(--cellpad) 20px;border-bottom:4px solid transparent;}
.case-choice[aria-pressed="true"] .case-choice-meta{border-bottom-color:var(--mint);}
.case-choice-meta .h3{display:block;margin-bottom:4px;font-size:22px;}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------- showcase (B2/C) */
.showcase-stage{display:grid;grid-template-columns:1fr;gap:1px;background:#000;}
/* H10 (R7): the showcase pins only where its side column fits. Below 561 px of height (768x432 = 200 % zoom) it takes the stacked layout, so no step text is clipped and the wheel never scrolls an inner panel. */
@media (min-width:768px) and (min-height:561px){ .showcase-stage{grid-template-columns:7fr 5fr;} }
.showcase-embed-cell{padding:0;background:var(--paper);position:relative;overflow:hidden;}
.showcase-embed-cell .showcase-frame-wrap{position:relative;width:100%;height:100%;overflow:hidden;background:var(--paper);}
.showcase-embed-cell .showcase-poster{position:absolute;inset:0;width:100%;height:100%;object-fit:contain;object-position:top center;}
.showcase-embed-cell iframe{
  position:absolute;top:0;left:0;width:1440px;height:900px;border:0;background:var(--paper);
  transform-origin:top left;pointer-events:none;opacity:0;
}
@media (max-width:767px), (max-height:560px){
  .showcase-embed-cell{position:sticky;top:48px;height:56svh;z-index:2;}
}
@media (min-width:768px) and (max-height:560px){ .showcase-embed-cell{height:45svh;} }
@media (min-width:768px) and (min-height:561px){
  /* R6 §3, two stacked causes, both fixed here:
     1) .showcase-side's natural content (all 5/6 rows, R5's rise-mask kept
        every body visible at once) was taller than the embed cell's
        explicit height. A CSS grid item with an explicit height does not
        stretch to match a taller sibling's row track - the TRACK grows to
        fit the tall side instead, leaving the embed cell short of the
        row's actual height by the difference (measured ~110px), exposing
        the stage's own black gap background below the frame. Pinning both
        columns to the SAME explicit height (with the side's own
        overflow-y:auto as a never-clip safety net) makes them structurally
        impossible to mismatch, regardless of how much text a future edit
        adds.
     2) That explicit height was `100svh - 48px`, sized to sit BELOW the
        48px sticky topline - but the pin (`start:'top top'`) puts the
        section's rendered top at the viewport's own y:0, with the topline
        merely painted on top of (not offsetting) its first 48px. The
        result: content correctly avoids the topline visually, but then
        runs 48px short of the viewport's bottom edge, showing the stage's
        black background as a trailing band under both columns (measured:
        embed/side bottom at 852 of a 900-tall viewport). Hero's own pin
        has this identical 48px arithmetic and gap - invisible there only
        because it lands on the page's own black background either side.
        Showcase's is visible because there's real content flush above it.
        Fixed the same way hero's is invisible: fill the FULL viewport
        (100svh) - the topline still visually covers the top 48px (it's
        position:sticky, z-index:40, opaque), but the bottom now lands
        exactly on the viewport edge, so no gap is left to expose.

     R7 runda 2, fynd 1: that "topline merely painted on top" claim was
     wrong for `.showcase-head`'s own rubrik - the topline IS opaque and
     DOES cover whatever renders in its first 48px; it just happened not to
     matter for hero (dark ground either side). Here `.showcase-head`'s
     headline-40 sits flush at the pinned section's very top edge, so its
     cap-height rendered UNDER the topline and got visually sheared (lead's
     through-05..through-12, 2026-09-25). Fix: pin the section 48px lower
     instead of hiding 48px under an opaque bar - `start:'top top+=48'` on
     the ScrollTrigger (setupDesktopEngine) puts the section's rendered top
     at y:48, exactly below the topline, and both cell heights shrink by
     the same 48px so the bottom still lands flush on the viewport edge -
     the R6 §3 gap this block fixed doesn't reopen, because now BOTH the
     offset and the height account for the topline, not just the height. */
  .showcase-embed-cell{height:calc(100svh - 48px);}
  .showcase-side{height:calc(100svh - 48px);overflow-y:auto;}
}
.showcase-side{display:grid;grid-template-rows:auto 1fr;gap:1px;background:#000;}
.showcase-panel{display:contents;}
.showcase-head{padding:calc(var(--cellpad)*1.4) var(--cellpad);color:var(--paper);}
/* H7: the frames are inert previews; the site itself opens from here */
.showcase-open{display:inline-flex;align-items:center;min-height:32px;margin-top:10px;font-size:16px;letter-spacing:-.01em;text-decoration:underline;text-underline-offset:3px;}
.showcase-open:focus-visible{outline:2px solid var(--paper);outline-offset:2px;}
.showcase-head .headline-40{margin-bottom:8px;}

/* R7 §C: the accordion ledger (R6 §1/§2) is replaced on desktop by a single
   crossfading box - one background for the whole "ruta", every step
   grid-stacked in one cell and GSAP-scrubbed by the showcase pin's onUpdate
   (never a class-toggle). Mobile keeps R6's stacked-rows layout unchanged;
   only its opacity mechanism changes (measured contrast fix, see below). */
.showcase-row{padding:var(--cellpad);display:flex;flex-direction:column;justify-content:center;}
.showcase-row h3{margin-bottom:0;}
.showcase-row p{max-width:52ch;font-size:15px;margin-top:8px;}

@media (min-width:768px) and (min-height:561px){
  /* R6 runda 6 (F-019/F-022): tre celler i sidans eget rutverk (gap:1px,
     background:#000 skiner igenom som fog, varje cell sin egen bakgrund) -
     räknarcellen (auto), textcellen (auto, satt av det längsta stegets
     höjd via samma grid-area:1/1-stapling som förut) och en ny detaljcell
     (1fr, fyller resten) som visar en bild ur den valda sajten per steg.
     Den lodräta stegskalan (R3-R4) är borttagen helt - Anton (F-022):
     "Det ser ut som något ofärdigt". Tom yta löses nu med riktigt innehåll
     (en bild ur arbetet), inte med ett dekorativt streck. */
  .showcase-rows{display:grid;grid-template-rows:auto auto 1fr;gap:1px;background:#000;height:100%;}
  .showcase-panel--calyx .showcase-box-head,
  .showcase-panel--calyx .showcase-steps{background:var(--paper);color:var(--ink);}
  .showcase-panel--horai .showcase-box-head,
  .showcase-panel--horai .showcase-steps{background:var(--black);color:var(--paper);}
  .showcase-panel--horai .showcase-row p{color:#bdbdbd;}
  /* räknarcellen: NN/NN överst, mintspåret under - som R3, innan R4 flyttade
     räknaren ned i den nu borttagna skalan. */
  .showcase-box-head{padding:var(--cellpad);}
  .showcase-counter{display:block;font-size:13px;margin-bottom:10px;}
  .showcase-track{position:relative;height:4px;}
  .showcase-track::before{content:'';position:absolute;top:50%;left:0;right:0;height:1px;background:#000;transform:translateY(-50%);}
  .showcase-panel--horai .showcase-track::before{background:var(--paper);opacity:.3;}
  .showcase-track-fill{position:absolute;top:0;left:0;width:100%;height:4px;background:var(--mint);transform-origin:0 50%;transform:scaleX(0);}
  .showcase-steps{display:grid;}
  /* R3 §4 (F-019): rubriken får aldrig ta över - sajten är huvudsaken,
     rutan är bildtexten. h3 tillbaka i rubrikskala (30px), inte
     headline-40-tokenet R2 lånade; jättesiffran är borttagen. */
  /* R6b: toppjusterad. Centrerad (basregeln) satte stegrubriken 14 px lägre i
     steg med tre rader än i steg med fyra, så rubriken hoppade vid varje byte. */
  .showcase-row{grid-area:1/1;padding:0 var(--cellpad) calc(var(--cellpad)*1.4);justify-content:flex-start;}
  .showcase-row h3{font-size:30px;line-height:1.15;font-weight:500;}
  .showcase-row p{font-size:18px;line-height:1.5;max-width:40ch;}
  /* detaljcellen: en <figure> per steg, grid-stackad (samma grid-area:1/1-
     teknik som .showcase-row ovan), färglager under och ett dither-rutnät
     ovanpå (buildTileGrid, samma mekanism som #kontakt/tes-bilden) som
     löses upp i den skrubbade pin-tidslinjen (C.tl, se buildStepTimelines).
     Calyx grå grund (dither svart-på-grått), Hōrai svart grund (dither
     vitt-på-svart) - samma två grundfärger dither.py redan producerar. */
  /* R6b: bilden är ett förstoringsglas (2,5-3x iframen) tagen i exakt cellens
     proportion vid 1440x900 (599,6/426,5 = 1,4058). Vid andra fönster varierar
     cellen från 0,63 (2560x1440) till 1,59 (1280x800); figuren låses därför
     till bildens proportion och passas in (contain) med container-enheter, så
     att färglagret och rutnätet ovanpå alltid täcker samma yta. Med cover
     klipptes luppen (adressen, priset) och rutorna gled ur linje mot färgen. */
  .showcase-detail{position:relative;overflow:hidden;min-height:0;container-type:size;}
  .showcase-panel--calyx .showcase-detail{background:var(--grey);}
  .showcase-panel--horai .showcase-detail{background:var(--black);}
  .showcase-figure{position:absolute;left:50%;top:50%;translate:-50% -50%;width:min(100cqw,140.58cqh);height:min(100cqh,71.13cqw);margin:0;opacity:0;}
  .showcase-figure:first-child{opacity:1;}
  .showcase-figure img{position:absolute;inset:0;width:100%;height:100%;object-fit:fill;}
}
@media (max-width:767px), (max-height:560px){
  /* R7 runda 2, fynd 2: .showcase-embed-cell (position:sticky) satt över
     .showcase-side (head + rader) i normalt dokumentflöde, så när huvudet
     ("Hōrai") rullade upp genom den redan-klistrade ramen (z-index:2) klipptes
     det mot ramens underkant (lead: through-02/03). Huvudet ska stå helt
     synligt INNAN raderna - och innan ramen - börjar klistra, så .showcase-side
     görs display:contents här (bara mobil) för att lyfta .showcase-head och
     .showcase-rows till .showcase-stage's egna grid-items, och ordnas om med
     `order`: huvud (1) -> ram (2, där klistringen börjar) -> rader (3). */
  .showcase-side{display:contents;}
  .showcase-head{order:1;}
  .showcase-embed-cell{order:2;}
  .showcase-rows{display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:1px;background:#000;order:3;}
  /* R6 runda 6: .showcase-box-head hålls INTE display:none längre. Mätt
     (shots/r6-mobile-before, före denna runda): den borttagna stegskalan
     (.showcase-scale) hade ALDRIG en egen mobilregel, så dess räknartext
     redan föll igenom osynligt formaterad, som en enkel textrad i
     .showcase-rows egen svarta gap-bakgrund, ovanpå .showcase-embed-cell.
     Räknaren (nu flyttad hit) måste fortsätta synas EXAKT så - briefen
     ("mobil oförändrad") gäller även denna oavsiktliga men redan existerande
     synlighet. .showcase-track har fortfarande ingen mobilstorlek (dess
     height/position-regler ligger kvar i 768px-blocket ovan) och kollapsar
     därför osynligt till 0px, precis som förut. */
  .showcase-detail{display:none;}
  .showcase-steps{display:contents;}
  .showcase-panel--calyx .showcase-row:nth-child(odd){background:var(--paper);}
  .showcase-panel--calyx .showcase-row:nth-child(even){background:var(--grey);}
  .showcase-panel--horai .showcase-row:nth-child(odd){background:var(--black);color:var(--paper);}
  .showcase-panel--horai .showcase-row:nth-child(odd) p{color:#bdbdbd;}
  .showcase-panel--horai .showcase-row:nth-child(even){background:var(--grey);}
}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------- pris */
.pris-statement{padding:calc(var(--cellpad)*2) var(--cellpad);}
.pris-statement .body-30{max-width:60ch;margin-top:16px;font-weight:500;}
/* All placement lives in these classes (not inline styles) so the media
   queries below can actually win the cascade at each breakpoint. */
.pris-bento{grid-template-columns:repeat(12,1fr);grid-template-rows:auto auto;}
.pris-lead{grid-column:1 / span 6;grid-row:1 / span 2;background:var(--mint);display:flex;flex-direction:column;justify-content:space-between;gap:24px;}
.pris-tier{display:flex;flex-direction:column;justify-content:space-between;gap:18px;min-height:220px;}
.pris-tier-a{grid-column:7 / span 6;grid-row:1;background:var(--paper);}
.pris-tier-b{grid-column:7 / span 6;grid-row:2;background:var(--grey);}
@media (max-width:1199px){
  .pris-bento{grid-template-columns:1fr 1fr;}
  .pris-lead{grid-column:1 / span 2;grid-row:1;}
  .pris-tier-a{grid-column:1;grid-row:2;}
  .pris-tier-b{grid-column:2;grid-row:2;}
}
@media (max-width:767px){
  .pris-bento{grid-template-columns:1fr;}
  .pris-lead,.pris-tier-a,.pris-tier-b{grid-column:1;grid-row:auto;min-height:0;}
}
.price-label{max-width:34ch;font-size:15px;}
.price-value{font-size:clamp(28px,3.6vw,44px);letter-spacing:-.03em;}
.price-value .unit{font-size:.5em;margin-left:2px;}
.price-value--text{font-size:clamp(18px,2vw,24px);}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------- kontakt (R5 §C: heron speglad) */
.kontakt-quad{
  position:relative;display:grid;gap:1px;background:#000;min-height:100svh;
  grid-template-columns:1fr 1fr;grid-template-rows:1fr 1fr;
  grid-template-areas:"ov oh" "nv nh";
}
.kontakt-q{position:relative;overflow:hidden;padding:var(--cellpad);}
.kontakt-q--ov{grid-area:ov;background:var(--black);color:var(--paper);display:flex;flex-direction:column;justify-content:flex-end;gap:10px;}
/* R6 §4: headline-40 is tuned for a single "jätteord" (hero, case names) -
   at this cell's half-page width, a four-word sentence in it ran past the
   ÖV/ÖH seam (measured x>720 at 1440, into the card's own space). A
   smaller, dedicated clamp - same family as the old kontakt-giant's - fits
   three lines comfortably inside the cell at 1440/1280/768, verified with
   getBoundingClientRect against the cell box, not eyeballed. */
.kontakt-q--ov h2{
  font-size:clamp(1.75rem, 1.1rem + 2.6vw, 3.4rem);line-height:1.05;
  letter-spacing:-.03em;font-weight:500;max-width:12ch;
}
.kontakt-q--ov p{max-width:32ch;font-size:15px;}
.kontakt-q--oh{grid-area:oh;background:var(--paper);}
.kontakt-q--nv{grid-area:nv;background:var(--grey);padding:0;}
.kontakt-q--nh{grid-area:nh;background:var(--mint);}
@media (max-width:767px){
  /* R6 §7: nh gets more room than ov/nv (was the same minmax(60vw) as
     both) - a 3D Y-axis rotation's perspective projection genuinely bulges
     a flat card's rendered bounding box taller at the near edge as it
     turns (measured: +/-28px top/bottom at 1200px perspective, still
     +/-24px at 3000px - foreshortening a rotated rectangle really does
     grow its axis-aligned bbox, not a rounding artefact), and centring an
     88%-wide card in a 60vw-tall row left only ~27px clearance to the
     subline above - not enough to survive that bulge at any angle in the
     0-180deg sweep. */
  .kontakt-quad{grid-template-columns:1fr;grid-template-rows:minmax(60vw,auto) minmax(76vw,auto) minmax(60vw,auto);grid-template-areas:"ov" "nh" "nv";min-height:auto;}
  .kontakt-q--oh{display:none;}
}

/* the card sits on the crossing of all four quadrants (a grid item that
   spans the full 2x2 and centres itself), mirroring heron's own card. On
   mobile it drops into the mint cell's own grid area instead, 88% wide. */
/* R6 §4/§7: centred on the FULL 2x2 crossing put the card's top edge only
   ~15-50px below the headline row at rest, with zero margin for the flip's
   lift or the hover-tilt's foreshortening - both could (and did, measured)
   bring the card within single-digit px of "verksamhet.". Spanning only
   the LOWER row (grid-row:2, still centred horizontally on the vertical
   seam = still "on the crossing") puts the card inside the NV/NH half
   entirely, with a full row-height of clearance above it before ÖV even
   starts. */
.kontakt-card-anchor{
  grid-column:1 / 3;grid-row:2;place-self:center;z-index:5;
  width:min(32vw,460px);aspect-ratio:85/55;perspective:1200px;
}
@media (max-width:767px){
  .kontakt-card-anchor{grid-area:nh;place-self:center;width:80%;}
}
.kontakt-card-tilt{width:100%;height:100%;position:relative;transform-style:preserve-3d;}
.card-flip2{width:100%;height:100%;position:relative;transform-style:preserve-3d;box-shadow:10px 10px 0 0 #000;}
.card-flip2 button.face{margin:0;padding:6%;font:inherit;text-align:left;cursor:pointer;display:block;width:100%;height:100%;}
.card-flip2 button.face:focus-visible{outline:2px solid var(--mint);outline-offset:2px;}
.face-back-hit{position:absolute;inset:0;z-index:0;background:transparent;border:0;padding:0;margin:0;cursor:pointer;}
.face-back-hit:focus-visible{outline:2px solid var(--mint);outline-offset:2px;}
.card-back-content{position:relative;z-index:1;height:100%;display:flex;flex-direction:column;justify-content:center;gap:10px;pointer-events:none;}
.card-back-content a{pointer-events:auto;}
.card-back-links{display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:6px;margin-top:4px;}
.card-back-links a{font-size:clamp(13px,1.5vw,18px);text-decoration:underline;width:max-content;}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------- footer */
.footer-cell{background:var(--black);color:var(--paper);padding:0 0 0 var(--cellpad);height:34vw;max-height:340px;min-height:200px;display:flex;align-items:flex-end;overflow:hidden;}
.footer-mark{font-size:clamp(80px,16vw,220px);line-height:.8;letter-spacing:-.04em;white-space:nowrap;padding-bottom:.06em;}
.footer-strip{padding:18px var(--cellpad);background:var(--black);color:var(--paper);}
.footer-strip a{text-decoration:underline;font-size:14px;}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------- resolve (dither -> color) */
.img-cell{position:relative;}
/* R3: §3 dither -> colour grid-stagger. The tile grid sits over the
   already-visible colour layer; each tile shows one slice of the dither
   image and fades on its own random-order schedule, so the resolve reads
   as pixels dissolving away rather than a wipe. Built once at init from
   the existing .dither-layer <img> (see buildTileGrid in the script). */
.tile-grid{position:absolute;inset:0;display:grid;pointer-events:none;}
.tile-grid > span{display:block;background-repeat:no-repeat;}
.is-resolving > .tile-grid > span{will-change:opacity;}
.color-layer{clip-path:none;}

/* R3: seam-anchored decorations, all created/positioned by the script. */
.seam-line{position:absolute;background:var(--mint);pointer-events:none;z-index:3;}
/* the crosshair seam-draw is a 2x2-grid flourish; hero-stage stacks to one
   column under 768px (see .hero-stage media query above), so the same
   absolute-positioned lines would otherwise bisect the whole stacked
   column top to bottom - hide them there. */
@media (max-width:767px){ .seam-line{display:none;} }
.process-row{position:relative;}
.process-progress{position:absolute;top:0;bottom:0;width:2px;background:var(--mint);transform:scaleY(0);transform-origin:top center;pointer-events:none;z-index:6;}
/* process-left/process-right only sit side by side at the 1200px+ 12-col
   grid (BYGGSPEC .g12 breakpoints); below that they stack, so the seam
   the progress line marks no longer exists - hide it rather than let a
   stale left-offset poke 2px past the right edge (390/768 overflow). */
@media (max-width:1199px){ .process-progress{display:none;} }

/* R3: SplitText's own mask:'lines'/'words'/'chars' option wraps each split
   unit in its own clipping span, and every heading that gets split already
   sits inside a .cell (overflow:hidden) or .footer-cell (overflow:hidden)
   — so no extra clip rule is needed on the headings themselves (adding one
   risked cutting descenders that round 2's static layout already relies
   on fitting without it). */

/* spacing rhythm between section groups */
.rhythm{height:110px;}
@media (max-width:767px){ .rhythm{height:72px;} }
</style>
</head>
